# MM-P1-L2-HT03-S1 Lubrication and fluids - Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #3
Revision: Rev E  
Plant: P1, line P1-L2  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L2-HT03  
This revision supersedes Rev D.

Scope
- Purpose: Define required lubricants, fluid handling, and quench timing control related to Ring Rolling heat treat furnace EQ-P1-L2-HT03.
- Applicability: Maintenance and reliability personnel responsible for routine and corrective lubrication and fluid services on EQ-P1-L2-HT03.
- Exclusions: This document does not cover process control programming, metallurgical cycle parameters, or furnace electrical systems beyond lubrication and fluids.

Background and rationale
- Proper lubrication and quench timing are critical to maintain mechanical reliability and to prevent unplanned downtime for EQ-P1-L2-HT03. Lubricant selection is driven by bearing types and the ambient oil-handling environment present on the furnace carriage and servomounts. Quench timing is monitored at the fluid delivery valve to ensure repeatable heat-treat outcomes and to protect mechanical components from thermal shock.
- The specified lubricant part number CFW-LUB-652 is selected for viscosity stability, oxidation resistance, and compatibility with seal materials used on the furnace. Field experience has shown reduced bearing wear when CFW-LUB-652 is applied per procedure.
- The quench delay maximum for Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P1-L2-HT03) is 24 seconds. This value is enforced as the maximum permissible delay between cycle completion and the start of fluid flow during quench sequences to reduce thermal gradients and avoid quench-related stress on mechanical mounting hardware.

Related documents
- SOP-P1-L2-01
- SOP-P1-L2-02
- SOP-P1-L2-03

Tools and materials
- Approved lubricant: CFW-LUB-652.
- Clean dispensing pump or sealed grease gun compatible with CFW-LUB-652.
- Lint-free wipes and solvent approved by maintenance chemistry group for seal cleaning.
- Fluid sampling bottles and labels for retention of lubricant samples.
- Personal protective equipment: oil-resistant gloves, eye protection, and shop apron.
- Lockout/tagout supplies as required by site safety procedures.
- Inspection mirror and borescope for visual inspection of hard-to-reach lubrication points.
- Torque and fastener tools are retained under separate documentation; refer to SOP-P1-L2-02 for mechanical fastening controls.

Procedure
- Preparation
  - Review current status of EQ-P1-L2-HT03 and consult SOP-P1-L2-01 for isolation requirements prior to any fluid service.
  - Place lockout/tagout on furnace motion and hydraulic sources in accordance with SOP-P1-L2-03.
  - Collect baseline condition: record current lubricant brand at sample point and visually inspect for contamination. Retain fluid sample in labeled bottle per site chemistry guidelines.
- Lubricant application
  - Clean lubrication fittings with lint-free wipe and approved solvent to remove external contamination.
  - Verify lubricant used on system is CFW-LUB-652. If previous fill differs, perform flush per site chemistry guidance before introducing CFW-LUB-652; record flush action in maintenance log.
  - Use a clean dispensing pump or sealed grease gun to deliver CFW-LUB-652 to each fitting until new, clean lubricant is observed at the return or vent point. Wipe excess and ensure no pooling occurs near electrical or hot surfaces.
  - For sealed units, inspect seals and replace if evidence of leakage or incompatibility is observed. Document seal part references in work order and reference SOP-P1-L2-02 for fastening practice when reassembling.
- Quench system verification
  - After lubricant service, verify quench valve actuation and timing sequence while system remains isolated from active heat cycles. Actuate quench control and measure delay from command to valve full open. The quench delay maximum for Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P1-L2-HT03) is 24 seconds. If measured delay exceeds 24 seconds, do not return the furnace to service; proceed to troubleshooting steps below.
- Troubleshooting (timing or contamination)
  - If quench delay exceeds specification: inspect actuator linkage, clean or replace control filters, and check for fluid contamination in control circuits. Replace filter elements per site filter change practice. Re-sample fluid and compare to baseline. Repeat timing verification.
  - If lubricant contamination is detected: isolate affected components, conduct controlled flush as per chemistry guidance, and replace lubricant with CFW-LUB-652 after confirming compatibility. Record contamination findings and corrective actions.
- Completion
  - Remove lockout/tagout and return EQ-P1-L2-HT03 to service only after successful timing verification and no evidence of leak or contamination.
  - Enter maintenance actions, parts used, and fluid sample IDs into the equipment maintenance record.

Acceptance criteria
- Lubrication: All lubrication points inspected during the activity must show fresh CFW-LUB-652 where applicable and no visible leaks at fittings or seals after reassembly.
- Quench timing: Measured delay from command to valve full open must be equal to or less than the quench delay maximum for Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P1-L2-HT03) is 24 seconds. Any measurement exceeding that value triggers follow-up troubleshooting and corrective action.
- Records: Work order must include lubricant part number used (CFW-LUB-652), sample IDs, inspection findings, and references to SOP-P1-L2-01, SOP-P1-L2-02, and SOP-P1-L2-03 as applicable.
- Sampling: Retained lubricant sample must be labeled and stored with the maintenance work order for the retention period defined by the site chemistry program.

Examples and records to keep
- Example entry in maintenance log: component serviced, lubricant CFW-LUB-652, sample bottle ID, quench timing test result, and reference to SOP-P1-L2-03 for isolation steps.
- Maintain a history file for EQ-P1-L2-HT03 documenting lubricant changeovers, contamination events, and timing anomalies with cross-reference to SOP-P1-L2-02 when mechanical replacement is performed.
- Non-conformance: If acceptance criteria are not met, create a corrective action record and tag equipment out of service until resolved.

Notes
- Coordinate any changes to lubricant specification with reliability engineering and site chemistry. Changes require revision control and cross-reference updates to SOP-P1-L2-01, SOP-P1-L2-02, and SOP-P1-L2-03.

# MM-P1-L2-RR01 - Maintenance manual - Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #1
Revision: Rev F  
Supersedes: Rev E  
Plant: P1, line P1-L2  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L2-RR01

Related documents: ECN-2026-041, SOP-P1-L2-01, SOP-P1-L2-04

Scope
This document defines preventive maintenance tasks, required tooling, stepwise procedure, and acceptance criteria for the Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #1 identified as EQ-P1-L2-RR01. It applies to maintenance technicians and engineers responsible for mechanical, lubrication, and fastener integrity tasks on this machine. Use this manual in conjunction with ECN-2026-041 for engineering changes and SOP-P1-L2-01 and SOP-P1-L2-04 for lockout/tagout and permit requirements.

Background and rationale
Ring rolling mills operate with high contact loads and tightly controlled clearances. Fastener preload and rolling element lubrication are primary contributors to reliable operation and dimensional control. The mandrel clamp joint secures tooling that transmits large axial and bending loads; correct bolt torque is required to maintain clamp stiffness and prevent slippage or galling. Bearing lubrication frequency controls grease condition and film thickness to prevent mixed or boundary lubrication, reducing wear and risk of subsurface fatigue. The procedures below focus on controlling these root causes of failure to minimize unplanned downtime and maintain process capability.

Required tools and materials
- Torque wrench calibrated per shop practice and traceable calibration records. Use a tool capable of achieving the specified torque for the mandrel clamp bolts.  
- Socket and drive set compatible with the clamp bolt head.  
- Clean lint-free rags and approved cleaning solvent.  
- Manufacturer-approved bearing lubricant for the main roll bearings.  
- Grease gun with clean coupler and reservoirs dedicated to bearing lubricant.  
- Maintenance log forms and history folder for EQ-P1-L2-RR01.  
- Personal protective equipment as required by SOP-P1-L2-01.

Critical values
- The mandrel clamp bolt torque for Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P1-L2-RR01) is 395 N·m.  
- The main roll bearing lubrication interval for Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P1-L2-RR01) is 175 hours.

Procedure
Preparation and safety
- Verify that the work area is clear of production material and that the machine is in the safe state required by SOP-P1-L2-01. Confirm electrical and mechanical isolation per SOP-P1-L2-04 before accessing clamp hardware or lubrication points.  
- Gather the tools and materials listed above. Record the equipment serial and location references in the maintenance log for EQ-P1-L2-RR01.

Mandrel clamp bolt torque verification and application
- Clean the clamp bolt head and surrounding surfaces with solvent and a lint-free rag to remove debris and old lubricants. Ensure threads visible for inspection are free of contamination.  
- Position the calibrated torque wrench and socket onto the clamp bolt head. Apply torque in a smooth, continuous motion until the wrench indicates the set value. Observe wrench behavior to ensure proper seating and avoid impact-style forcing.  
- If multiple clamp bolts are present in the clamp assembly, sequence torque application using an alternating pattern to avoid introducing clamp distortion. Repeat final torque verification on all bolts after the sequence is complete.  
- Document the tool identification, torque value applied, technician name, and any anomalies such as thread damage, coating loss, or bolt elongation in the maintenance record for EQ-P1-L2-RR01.

Main roll bearing lubrication
- Confirm access to the bearing grease fittings and clean the fitting area to prevent contamination during lubrication. Inspect seals and housings for visible damage before lubricant application.  
- Use the approved lubricant and grease gun. Apply lubricant until a small amount is observed at the bearing seals or per bearing manufacturer guidance, taking care not to overpack. If resistance increases sharply during pumping, stop and inspect for potential blockage.  
- Record the lubricant lot number, grease quantity dispensed if measured by pump counts, and the start/stop time in the equipment lubrication log. Update the running hours counter for main roll bearing lubrication interval on the EQ-P1-L2-RR01 maintenance tracker.

Inspection and corrective actions
- After torque and lubrication tasks, perform a visual inspection of adjacent components for signs of leakage, looseness, or contamination. Rotate the mandrel or rolls slowly as required to confirm free movement without abnormal noise or binding.  
- If any component fails inspection or if bolt threads or bearing seals show damage, tag the component out of service and notify maintenance supervision and engineering per ECN-2026-041 for disposition. Record corrective actions taken and parts replaced in the equipment history.

Examples and records to keep
- Example entry for clamp torque action: specify the equipment id EQ-P1-L2-RR01, date, technician initials, tool id, applied torque 395 N·m, and observations. Attach any photographs of bolt condition.  
- Example entry for bearing lubrication: specify equipment id EQ-P1-L2-RR01, lubricant id, grease lot number, start/stop time, and note main roll bearing lubrication interval reference 175 hours. Include next due hours value in the maintenance planner.  
- Maintain a folder for EQ-P1-L2-RR01 containing torque certificates, calibration records for torque wrench, grease certification, and copies of any ECN-2026-041 change forms that affect clamp or bearing systems.

Acceptance criteria
- Mandrel clamp bolts must show no visual thread damage, must be seated flush without gaps attributable to improperly installed washers or debris, and must be verified at the specified torque value recorded as 395 N·m. Any bolt that does not reach the specified torque due to deformation or stripping must be removed and replaced prior to machine return to service.  
- Main roll bearings must show adequate lubricant presence at seals or meet manufacturer criteria after service and maintenance records must reflect the main roll bearing lubrication interval 175 hours. Bearings that exhibit elevated running noise, excess heat, or visible lubricant degradation must be escalated for bearing teardown and evaluation per ECN-2026-041.  
- All maintenance entries for EQ-P1-L2-RR01 must include technician identification, tool calibration references, and linkage to SOP-P1-L2-01 and SOP-P1-L2-04 where lockout and permit actions were required.

Revision and change control
All deviations, repairs, or engineering substitutions must reference ECN-2026-041 and be recorded under the EQ-P1-L2-RR01 equipment history before returning the machine to production.

# MM-P1-L4-HT03 — Maintenance manual - Heat Treat heat treat furnace #3
Revision: Rev D  
This revision supersedes Rev C.

Plant: P1, line P1-L4  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L4-HT03

Scope
- This document defines preventive and corrective maintenance procedures for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P1-L4-HT03) used in the austenitizing and quench portion of the P1-L4 line. It applies to maintenance technicians and process engineers responsible for furnace integrity, thermal control, and thermocouple accuracy.
- The objective is to maintain process capability and safety by preserving setpoint accuracy and sensor reliability. The austenitizing setpoint for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P1-L4-HT03) is 880 °C. The thermocouple calibration interval for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P1-L4-HT03) is 75 days.
- Reference related documents for engineering changes, safety bulletins, and standard operating procedures: ECN-2026-002, SB-1006, SOP-P1-L4-02.

Tools
- Portable data logger with calibrated input compatible with furnace thermocouples.
- Reference thermocouple assembly traceable to laboratory standard.
- Hand tools for access panel removal and sensor replacement.
- Contact cleaner rated for high-temperature sensor connectors.
- Inspection flashlight, mirror, and personal protective equipment appropriate for thermal and electrical hazards.
- Lockout/tagout kit and multimeter for continuity checks.
- Calibration records binder or maintenance electronic record entry system.

Background and rationale
- Regular verification of thermocouple performance and control setpoint stability is essential to ensure the austenitizing stage reaches metallurgical targets without overexposure. Drift in sensor readings or controller setpoint deviation can cause inconsistent microstructure and part rejection.
- The austenitizing setpoint for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P1-L4-HT03) is 880 °C; maintaining that setpoint within acceptable process control limits depends on reliable thermocouple readings and controller tuning. Calibrating thermocouples at the interval specified reduces the likelihood of long-term drift affecting process outcomes.
- The thermocouple calibration interval for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P1-L4-HT03) is 75 days. This interval balances sensor aging rates observed in production with acceptable administrative workload and aligns maintenance frequency with process risk.

Procedure
- Preparation
  - Notify production and obtain authorization per SOP-P1-L4-02 before starting maintenance. Review ECN-2026-002 for any recent engineering changes that affect furnace wiring or sensor types. Consult SB-1006 for any safety bulletins relevant to this equipment.
  - Execute lockout/tagout and follow site electrical isolation protocols before removing access panels or disconnecting thermocouple leads.

- Thermocouple inspection and calibration
  - Visually inspect thermocouple sheath and connection points for physical damage, corrosion, or loose fittings. Clean connectors using contact cleaner if contamination is present.
  - Disconnect thermocouple assembly and install reference thermocouple assembly into the same location. Connect the portable data logger and bring the furnace through a controlled heat sequence sufficient to reach the austenitizing region while complying with production requirements and safety guidance in SOP-P1-L4-02.
  - Record temperature readings from both the furnace controller and the reference thermocouple at representative points in the thermal profile, with particular attention near the austenitizing setpoint. Verify that the controller reading corresponds to the reference within acceptable deviation determined by process engineering. If readings are outside acceptable deviation, tag the sensor for replacement and proceed to corrective actions.
  - Reinstall original thermocouple after verification. If replacement is required, remove the old thermocouple and install a new unit of matching type and configuration per ECN-2026-002. Reconnect and verify continuity with a multimeter prior to energizing.

- Controller setpoint verification
  - With thermocouple confirmed, verify controller is set to the austenitizing setpoint for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P1-L4-HT03) of 880 °C. Confirm that controller parameters match documented process parameters in SOP-P1-L4-02 and that no unauthorized changes exist.
  - Perform a controlled heat cycle to the austenitizing region and monitor temperature stability at setpoint for an appropriate dwell period consistent with process needs. Observe for oscillation or steady-state drift and document any anomalies to be addressed by process engineering.

- Corrective actions and documentation
  - If thermocouple calibration is out of tolerance or controller discrepancy exists, replace or recalibrate equipment, and retest until readings meet acceptance criteria. Record the nature of the fault, corrective actions taken, replacement part description, and the technician performing the work.
  - Enter calibration results and maintenance actions into the electronic record system and log the next due calibration based on the thermocouple calibration interval for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P1-L4-HT03) of 75 days.
  - Return the furnace to service following verification and remove lockout/tagout devices per site procedure.

Acceptance criteria
- Thermocouple verification
  - Reference thermocouple and furnace controller readings at and near the austenitizing setpoint must agree within the tolerance defined in SOP-P1-L4-02. Readings must demonstrate no unexplained drift during the verification cycle.
- Setpoint confirmation
  - Controller must be set to the austenitizing setpoint for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P1-L4-HT03) of 880 °C and maintain stable temperature control around that setpoint during the verification heat cycle.
- Documentation
  - Maintenance record must include: equipment id EQ-P1-L4-HT03, a statement that the austenitizing setpoint for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P1-L4-HT03) is 880 °C, confirmation that the thermocouple calibration interval for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P1-L4-HT03) is 75 days and the next due date per that interval, copy of raw logger data, description of any corrective actions, and references to ECN-2026-002, SB-1006, SOP-P1-L4-02.
- Example records to keep
  - Calibration worksheet with paired readings from controller and reference thermocouple.
  - Photographs of installed thermocouple and connector condition if replaced.
  - Signed maintenance entry with technician identifier and notes on any deviations and follow-up recommendations.

Notes and follow-up
- Any recurring deviations or failures should trigger an engineering review and possible scope change via ECN-2026-002. Safety-related observations must be reported under SB-1006. Follow SOP-P1-L4-02 for coordination with production and process tracking.

# MM-P2-L1-RR01 - Maintenance manual - Hot Forge radial ring rolling mill #1
Revision: Rev B (This revision supersedes Rev A)

Plant: P2, line P2-L1  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L1-RR01

Scope
This document provides maintenance instructions for Hot Forge radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P2-L1-RR01). It covers preventive maintenance tasks required to preserve functional performance of the drive train, mandrel clamp, main roll bearings, lubrication systems, and safety interlocks. Tasks are intended for qualified maintenance personnel familiar with heavy forging equipment and the site safety program. Refer to related engineering change and operating procedures for context: ECN-2026-023, SOP-P2-L1-01, SOP-P2-L1-02.

Background and rationale
The radial ring rolling mill is subject to cyclic loading, high contact stresses, and thermal influences inherent to hot forging operations. Key failure modes observed historically include bearing fatigue, loss of clamp preload, and lubricant degradation. Preventive maintenance focuses on maintaining clamp torque and bearing lubrication to extend service life and reduce unplanned downtime. Records and rationale for tolerances are kept in the equipment history file and are intended to support trend analysis and ECN decisions.

Tools and materials
- Calibrated torque wrench sized to apply the prescribed clamp torque to mandrel clamp bolts on EQ-P2-L1-RR01.
- Clean rags and approved solvent for degreasing contact areas.
- Manufacturer-approved lubricant for main roll bearings and grease gun or centralized lube access tools compatible with supplied grease fittings.
- Bearing puller and drift set for bearing replacement operations where applicable.
- Safety lockout/tagout kit and personal protective equipment per site rules.
- Inspection mirror and borescope for visual evaluation of internal surfaces.
- Maintenance log forms and digital entry device for records.

Procedure
Preparation
- Place the mill in the maintenance state following SOP-P2-L1-01 and SOP-P2-L1-02. Ensure all energy sources are isolated and the machine is tagged out and blocked against motion. Confirm authorization to proceed per site lockout/tagout.
- Consult ECN-2026-023 for any recent engineering changes that affect components, fasteners, or lubrication scheme on EQ-P2-L1-RR01.

Mandrel clamp bolt torque verification
- Clean bolt heads and access areas so torque readings are accurate. Remove paint or sealant that interferes with wrench seating.
- Using the calibrated torque wrench, apply torque to mandrel clamp bolts to achieve 430 N·m. This is the specified clamping torque for EQ-P2-L1-RR01 mandrel clamp bolts.
- If bolts rotate before achieving the specified torque, mark as loose and inspect for stripped threads or damaged fastener. Replace damaged fasteners and reapply to specified torque.
- Record bolt identification, final torque value, and inspector initials in the maintenance log and the equipment history file.

Main roll bearing lubrication
- Verify lubricant condition and level before replenishment. Follow lubricant manufacturer guidance and ECN-2026-023 for approved grease type.
- Lubricate main roll bearings per the lubrication scheme for EQ-P2-L1-RR01. The main roll bearing lubrication interval for Hot Forge radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P2-L1-RR01) is 275 hours. Use this interval as the planning basis for scheduling and for updating run-hour counters.
- When applying grease, purge using the grease fittings until purged material appears clean at relief points, indicating circulation through the bearing cavity. Avoid over-greasing; allow expelled material to be captured on a clean rag or container.
- Document lubricant batch, date, hours at change, and technician performing the task.

Inspection and corrective actions
- Inspect bearing housings for signs of leakage, scoring, abnormal wear, or overheating discoloration. Use borescope to review internal raceways where accessible.
- Check mandrel clamp for even seating and absence of radial play after torque verification. If uneven clamping is detected, disassemble clamp components and inspect for wear or deformation.
- For bearings exhibiting noise, vibration, or visible damage, escalate to bearing replacement workflow. Use bearing puller and replacement parts compatible with EQ-P2-L1-RR01 as listed in the equipment parts file and ECN-2026-023.
- After any corrective replacement, reapply the required mandrel clamp bolt torque of 430 N·m and restart lubrication per the established interval of 275 hours.

Records to keep
- Maintenance log entry detailing work performed, readings observed, parts installed, lubricant batch numbers, and condition notes. Store in the equipment history file for EQ-P2-L1-RR01.
- A torque verification tag attached to the mandrel clamp assembly indicating the date and signature of the person who applied 430 N·m torque.
- Lubrication register entries that capture the run-hour reading at time of lubrication and the notation that the main roll bearing lubrication interval for Hot Forge radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P2-L1-RR01) is 275 hours was observed and applied.
- Any deviation reports and follow-up corrective action records referenced to ECN-2026-023.

Acceptance criteria
- Mandrel clamp bolts must show no visible motion under moderate manual force after application of 430 N·m torque, and clamp geometry must be within acceptable alignment documented in the equipment file.
- Main roll bearings must present no abnormal vibration or noise during a controlled slow-speed rotation after maintenance and must run within acceptable temperature band as defined in the equipment operating limits in the equipment file. Lubrication must be completed and recorded in accordance with the main roll bearing lubrication interval for Hot Forge radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P2-L1-RR01) is 275 hours.
- All maintenance actions must be recorded in the equipment history file and signed by the performing technician and the supervising engineer. Any failure to meet acceptance criteria triggers a hold condition until corrective actions are completed and reinspection confirms compliance.

References
- ECN-2026-023
- SOP-P2-L1-01
- SOP-P2-L1-02

Notes
Maintain traceability of torque wrench calibration certificates and lubricant certificates in the equipment maintenance folder for EQ-P2-L1-RR01. This manual revision updates procedures superseding Rev A and must be used for all subsequent maintenance events.
title: Maintenance manual - Hot Forge radial ring rolling mill #1

# MM-P2-L3-RR01-S1 — Lubrication and fluids - Machining radial ring rolling mill #1
Revision: Rev D (this revision supersedes Rev C)
Plant: P2, line P2-L3
Equipment: EQ-P2-L3-RR01

Scope
This document defines lubrication and fluid handling requirements for Machining radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P2-L3-RR01) in plant P2, line P2-L3. It covers lubricant selection, supply system checks, fill and drain procedure, contamination control, and record keeping for machining and bearing lubrication points associated with this equipment. This maintenance manual is intended for maintenance technicians, reliability engineers, and shift leaders who perform or supervise fluid servicing tasks. Refer to MM-P2-L3-RR01, SB-1036, and SOP-P2-L3-05 for related electrical lockout requirements, material safety guidance, and mill operating constraints.

Background and rationale
Effective lubrication prevents premature wear, maintains dimensional stability of rings during machining, and reduces the risk of fluid-related contamination in downstream processes. The maximum ring outer diameter for Machining radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P2-L3-RR01) is 1115 mm. Lubricant selection and handling must protect machine components while remaining compatible with workpiece metallurgical requirements and downstream cleaning processes. The lubricant specified for the machine is supplied under part number CFW-LUB-225; use only this part number for replenishment to ensure chemical compatibility and warranty compliance.

Tools
- Clean fluid transfer pump or dispensing nozzle compatible with CFW-LUB-225 and with nonmetallic seals.
- Approved containers for storage and waste that meet SB-1036 requirements and show the part number CFW-LUB-225 on labels.
- Clean lint‑free rags and particle-free funnels for fluid transfer.
- Inspection mirror and flashlight for visual checks of reservoirs, lines, and seals.
- Sample bottles and labels for fluid analysis; label each sample with machine id EQ-P2-L3-RR01 and location.
- Personal protective equipment per SB-1036 and SOP-P2-L3-05.

Procedure
Preparation
- Confirm that work is authorized per SOP-P2-L3-05 and that electrical and mechanical isolation is in place per facility lockout procedures referenced in MM-P2-L3-RR01.
- Verify that the supply stock matches part number CFW-LUB-225 before opening any containers. Do not mix alternate fluids or unidentified material with system fluid.

Drain and inspection
- Isolate the system and position waste containment to capture all drained fluid. Using clean transfer equipment, drain the reservoirs and primary sumps to waste containers labeled with CFW-LUB-225 as applicable.
- Visually inspect drained fluid for contamination indicators such as particulate, color change, or phase separation. Collect a representative sample in an approved bottle and label it with the equipment id EQ-P2-L3-RR01 and drain location for lab analysis if contamination is suspected.

Cleaning and component check
- Wipe accessible reservoir interiors with lint‑free rags until no visible build up remains. Inspect seals, sight glasses, and filters for damage or excessive wear. Replace damaged items before refilling; consult MM-P2-L3-RR01 for parts identification.
- Check supply lines and fittings for leaks. Tighten fittings to secure-but-not-overstressed condition; if threads or fittings are damaged, replace them per MM-P2-L3-RR01 parts guidance.

Refill
- Filter incoming supply through an approved filter media compatible with CFW-LUB-225 during transfer. Pour or pump fluid into reservoirs gently to minimize aeration. Use labeled funnels and clean hose assemblies exclusively reserved for CFW-LUB-225 to avoid cross-contamination.
- Operate the lubrication system at low speed per SOP-P2-L3-05 until fluid circulates and air pockets are purged. Observe sight glasses and check for external leaks. If foaming or persistent aeration is observed, stop and investigate before resuming.

Post-service verification
- Run the machine through a no-load verification routine per SOP-P2-L3-05 to confirm lubrication flow to bearings and slides. Monitor for abnormal noise or vibration; if present, isolate and investigate.
- Complete system level checks and mark reservoirs with the date of service and the technician's name in the maintenance log.

Examples and special cases
- When machining rings near the maximum allowed outer diameter of 1115 mm special attention must be given to coolant containment and chip separation to limit contaminant ingress into lubrication reservoirs. Modify guards and chip flow paths as necessary to prevent swarf from entering fluid returns.
- If unexpected contamination is found in a collected sample, follow the escalation path in MM-P2-L3-RR01 for analysis and corrective action. Retain samples and records until analysis is complete.

Contamination control and waste handling
- Store CFW-LUB-225 in sealed containers and restrict transfer equipment use to this lubricant only. Label storage with the part number CFW-LUB-225 and equipment id EQ-P2-L3-RR01 where dedicated supply is located.
- Waste fluids and contaminated rags must be handled and disposed of according to SB-1036. Maintain waste manifests and disposal receipts in the maintenance file.

Acceptance criteria
- Reservoirs and lubrication delivery lines must show no visible contamination after servicing and no unplanned leaks during no-load verification run. Bearings and moving interfaces must receive lubricant flow as verified during post-service checks described in SOP-P2-L3-05.
- Only fluid matching part number CFW-LUB-225 may be present in the system after service. Any deviation requires immediate reporting and corrective action as defined in MM-P2-L3-RR01.
- Records must include the technician name, equipment id EQ-P2-L3-RR01, lubricant part number CFW-LUB-225, sample identifiers, and a concise description of any anomalies. Store records in the equipment maintenance file and reference them in future service activities.

Records to keep
- Service log entry referencing this document id MM-P2-L3-RR01-S1 and related document ids MM-P2-L3-RR01, SB-1036, SOP-P2-L3-05.
- Sample labels and laboratory results when contamination is suspected.
- Waste disposal documentation per SB-1036 requirements.
- Inspection checklists and post-service verification notes retained with the EQ-P2-L3-RR01 maintenance file.

References
- MM-P2-L3-RR01
- SB-1036
- SOP-P2-L3-05

# MM-P3-L2-HT03 - Maintenance manual - Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #3
Revision: Rev C — This revision supersedes Rev B  
Plant: P3, line P3-L2  
Equipment: EQ-P3-L2-HT03

Scope
This document describes mandatory preventative and corrective maintenance tasks for Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P3-L2-HT03) used in the P3, line P3-L2 heat treat cell. It covers background, rationale for actions, required tools, step-by-step procedure for common maintenance activities, examples of typical findings with recommended responses, and records to retain. This manual is intended for qualified maintenance technicians and process engineers responsible for the operation and reliability of EQ-P3-L2-HT03. Related documents: SB-1015, SB-1041, SOP-P3-L2-01.

Background and rationale
EQ-P3-L2-HT03 is used for austenitizing and quenching of ring rolling forgings. Maintaining furnace atmosphere control, element integrity, and sensor accuracy is critical to ensure metallurgical consistency. The austenitizing setpoint for Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P3-L2-HT03) is 870 °C. Accurate temperature control at that setpoint ensures a consistent microstructure prior to quench and reduces rework risk. Thermocouple drift and wiring faults are common causes of setpoint deviations and must be addressed proactively; the thermocouple calibration interval for Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P3-L2-HT03) is 65 days. Calibration and verification of the control chain prevent undetected excursions that can affect part properties.

Tools
- Portable calibrated temperature indicator with ITS-90 traceability and probe compatible with furnace compensating circuit.  
- Thermocouple splice kit and insulation rated for furnace service.  
- Insulating gloves and face protection rated for high-temperature maintenance tasks.  
- Hand tools required for thermocouple access panels and furnace element access panels.  
- Lint-free cloths and contact cleaner suitable for electrical use.  
- Accessory logs and the furnace maintenance checklist form from SOP-P3-L2-01.  
- Records binder or electronic folder for maintenance entries and calibration certificates.

Procedure
General notes: All activities must follow applicable lockout/tagout practice and local safety rules. Perform visual inspections before entering any confined enclosure. Refer to SB-1015 and SB-1041 for safety bulletins and specific hazard controls.

Initial verification
- Confirm the furnace is empty of load and at a safe state per SOP-P3-L2-01.  
- Review the maintenance log for the past entries and for the last thermocouple calibration certificate. Confirm the thermocouple calibration interval for Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P3-L2-HT03) is being tracked per schedule.

Thermocouple verification and calibration
- Isolate furnace controls and access thermocouple junction box. Inspect wiring for chafing, oxidation, and secure terminations. Clean contacts with contact cleaner. Rationale: poor connections introduce measurement offsets and intermittent readings.  
- Attach portable calibrated indicator to the thermocouple compensation circuit and record steady-state deviation at multiple setpoints during a controlled heat cycle to the austenitizing setpoint. Compare readings against control panel display. Rationale: verifying at control-relevant setpoints ensures calibration covers the operational range. The austenitizing setpoint for Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P3-L2-HT03) is 870 °C; ensure the control and probe agreement at or near this setpoint.  
- If deviation exceeds the allowed tolerance in SOP-P3-L2-01, replace the thermocouple assembly and re-test. Record the service action. Rationale: addressing out-of-tolerance thermocouples eliminates systematic offsets that compromise part quality.

Element and refractory inspection
- Inspect visible heating elements for discoloration consistent with age or mechanical contact. Inspect element mounts and fasteners for deformation. Rationale: mechanical damage reduces element life and causes uneven heating.  
- Inspect refractory surfaces for spalling or cracks that expose anchors or support structures. Minor surface defects should be documented; significant breaches that affect insulation integrity require escalated repair per SB-1041. Rationale: refractory damage increases heat loss and creates hot or cold spots.

Control system checks
- With the furnace isolated, inspect control cabinet for loose terminals, dust accumulation, and proper ventilation. Clean as required. Rationale: dust and vibration lead to intermittent control faults.  
- Verify alarm setpoints and logger status against SOP-P3-L2-01. Confirm that the data acquisition system is archiving to the designated folder.

Examples of findings and responses
- Example: Control display reads lower than portable indicator at 870 °C. Response: Document delta, replace thermocouple if outside SOP-P3-L2-01 tolerance, re-calibrate, and run verification cycle.  
- Example: Hairline refractory crack across crown. Response: Photograph, log as condition report per SB-1015, schedule repair if crack compromises insulation continuity.  
- Example: Loose terminal discovered in control cabinet. Response: Secure terminal, record action, and perform a 100% functional checkout.

Records to keep
- Completed maintenance checklist from SOP-P3-L2-01 for each maintenance visit.  
- Thermocouple calibration certificates and verification logs showing comparisons to furnace control display. Ensure the thermocouple calibration interval for Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P3-L2-HT03) is documented and dates recorded.  
- Photographs of defects and condition reports referenced to SB-1015 and SB-1041 as applicable.  
- Signed technician entry noting parts replaced, serial numbers if available, and confirmation of functional tests.

Acceptance criteria
- Temperature control validation: Control panel and portable calibrated indicator agree within the allowable tolerance defined in SOP-P3-L2-01 at the austenitizing setpoint of 870 °C. Rationale: agreement at the working setpoint validates the measurement chain used for production runs.  
- Thermocouple status: The thermocouple calibration interval for Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P3-L2-HT03) is enforced; calibration certificate present and dated within the interval tracking.  
- Element and refractory condition: No exposed anchors or insulation breaches that create safety hazards or uncontrolled heat loss; minor spalls logged and scheduled for repair; major defects escalated per SB-1041.  
- Control cabinet: No unsecured terminals, no abnormal alarms upon restart, and data logging resumed.

Revision and distribution
This manual is maintained under the plant document control system. Refer to SOP-P3-L2-01 for forms and checklists. Related documents: SB-1015, SB-1041, SOP-P3-L2-01.

# MM-P3-L4-HT02 - Maintenance manual - Heat Treat heat treat furnace #2
Revision: Rev F  
Plant: P3, line P3-L4  
Equipment: EQ-P3-L4-HT02  
This revision supersedes Rev E.

Scope
This document provides maintenance procedures for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P3-L4-HT02). It covers preventive maintenance actions, verification steps after repair, and required records for the heat treat process critical to metallurgical integrity. The procedures herein apply to EQ-P3-L4-HT02 located on line P3-L4 and are intended for qualified maintenance technicians and furnace operators. Related documents: ECN-2026-001, SOP-P3-L4-02, SOP-P3-L4-05.

Background and rationale
The heat treat furnace is used to achieve required metallurgical phases before downstream operations. Correct furnace control and sensor accuracy are essential to ensure repeatable results and to avoid scrap or rework. The austenitizing setpoint for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P3-L4-HT02) is 885 °C. Sensor drift or control element degradation can shift achieved temperatures away from setpoint; therefore, planned checks and calibration are required. Thermocouple performance affects temperature control and records; the thermocouple calibration interval for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P3-L4-HT02) is 130 days.

Tools and materials
Use only calibrated electrical test equipment and documented calibration sources. Typical tools include insulated hand tools, appropriate personal protective equipment for high-temperature work, furnace door lift aids as installed by plant, replacement thermocouple assemblies specified in maintenance spares, and data capture devices compatible with plant historian. Consult SOP-P3-L4-02 and SOP-P3-L4-05 for personal protective equipment and lockout-tagout steps.

Procedure
Overview
Perform preventive maintenance and verification during scheduled downtime only. Follow plant lockout-tagout procedures before accessing furnace internal components. Refer to ECN-2026-001 for approved engineering changes before performing mechanical modifications.

Pre-maintenance verification
Confirm that the furnace is at ambient condition and isolated from electrical and gas supplies per SOP-P3-L4-02. Verify that the operator log indicates no active cycles. Ensure that data logging for the last run is archived and stored with maintenance records.

Thermocouple verification and calibration
Inspect thermocouple sheath and connection points for mechanical damage and contamination. If visible damage is found, replace the thermocouple assembly using the spare specified by maintenance spares and document the replacement. Calibrate thermocouples against a traceable reference. The thermocouple calibration interval for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P3-L4-HT02) is 130 days. Record raw calibration readings and correction factors in the maintenance log and in the furnace sensor calibration record.

Control loop check and setpoint verification
With the furnace isolated and safe to operate per SOP-P3-L4-05, power the control system to diagnostic mode. Verify that control outputs respond to command changes and that actual temperature readback corresponds to simulated inputs. Confirm that the control system maintains the austenitizing setpoint for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P3-L4-HT02) is 885 °C. If the control loop does not track as expected, troubleshoot actuator elements and sensors; document corrective actions and reference ECN-2026-001 if hardware changes are required.

Element and refractory inspection
Inspect heating elements for physical integrity and refractory for spalling or cracks. Document any defects and replace according to approved parts lists. After element replacement, verify resistance continuity and confirm that installation does not obstruct thermocouple placement.

Post-maintenance verification
Restore power and control functions following SOP-P3-L4-02. Run a controlled heat up to verify stable control and data capture. Compare recorded temperature profile against the expected profile with particular attention to the austenitizing setpoint for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P3-L4-HT02) is 885 °C. Validate that thermocouple corrections applied from the latest calibration produce accurate process records.

Acceptance criteria
Equipment acceptance is based on a combination of documented inspections, successful function checks, and calibration records. Acceptance requires the following:
- No visible mechanical defects or electrical hazards remain following maintenance.
- Thermocouple calibration records demonstrate that corrections have been applied and are traceable to plant calibration standards; thermocouple maintenance meets the thermocouple calibration interval for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P3-L4-HT02) is 130 days.
- Control system is capable of maintaining and recording the austenitizing setpoint for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P3-L4-HT02) is 885 °C during verification runs.
- All deviations found during maintenance have documented corrective actions and have been signed off by authorized maintenance personnel.

Records and example entries
Maintain a maintenance folder for EQ-P3-L4-HT02 that contains the following records and example entries:
- Work order with a brief description of actions performed and a reference to this document id MM-P3-L4-HT02.
- Thermocouple calibration certificate showing before and after readings and the date of calibration; include traceability to plant calibration standards.
- Control loop test log with simulated input values and actual output responses; include corrective action notes if adjustments were required.
- Refractory and heating element inspection report with photographs of defects and replacement part serials where applicable.
- Final verification report showing that the austenitizing setpoint for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P3-L4-HT02) is 885 °C was achieved and recorded.

Examples and notes
Example entries in the thermocouple record should include raw measured values, applied offsets, and a note stating that calibration meets the thermocouple calibration interval for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P3-L4-HT02) is 130 days. Example control loop logs should show the commanded output and the measured temperature trace demonstrating stable control around the austenitizing setpoint for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P3-L4-HT02) is 885 °C.

References

SOP-P3-L4-02
SOP-P3-L4-05

# MM-P3-L4-HT02-S2 - Fastener inspection and torque - Heat Treat heat treat furnace #2
Revision: Rev F (this revision supersedes Rev E)  
Plant: P3, line P3-L4  
Equipment: EQ-P3-L4-HT02

Scope
This document establishes the required fastener inspection and torque verification practices for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P3-L4-HT02). It covers inspection rationale, permitted tools, step-by-step procedure for visual and functional checks during preventive maintenance and reactive servicing, and clear acceptance criteria. This procedure supports safe mechanical integrity and repeatable process conditions that affect quench timing and furnace seals. See related documents MM-P3-L4-HT02, SB-1043, SOP-P3-L4-01 for broader maintenance schedules, safety bulletins, and furnace operating procedures.

Background and rationale
Fasteners on EQ-P3-L4-HT02 secure components that influence alignment of quench delivery, furnace door seals, shielding, and mounting of sensors. Loose or improperly lubricated fasteners can permit movement that alters quench timing and introduces variability into heat treat cycles. Fastener threads that bind or gall can lead to under-torqued joints even when torque tools indicate target settings. Visual inspection combined with torque verification and proper lubrication reduces unplanned downtime, improves repeatability, and protects threaded components from wear.

Tools
- Calibrated torque wrench (see calibration records per SOP-P3-L4-01).  
- Clean, lint-free rags and inspection mirror.  
- Thread lubricant: The lubricant part number for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P3-L4-HT02) is CFW-LUB-371.  
- Thread cleaning tools (non-abrasive brushes, compressed air per SB-1043).  
- Fastener identification tags and maintenance log forms.  
- Personal protective equipment per SOP-P3-L4-01.

Procedure
Preparation
- Review furnace history in MM-P3-L4-HT02 and confirm required maintenance window with operations. Lockout and de-energize as required by SOP-P3-L4-01 before accessing structural fasteners, door hardware, sensor mounts, and quench manifold connections.
- Gather required tools and lubricant CFW-LUB-371. Verify torque wrench calibration status per SOP-P3-L4-01.

Visual inspection
- Inspect all accessible external and internal fasteners for thread damage, corrosion, or evidence of movement (fretting, imprinting). Use an inspection mirror for hard-to-see locations.
- Check for missing fastener hardware or non-standard replacements. Tag any non-standard hardware and report per MM-P3-L4-HT02.
- Inspect mating faces and plug interfaces for burrs or debris that would prevent proper clamp-up. Clean with lint-free rags and approved cleaning procedures referenced in SB-1043.

Thread and bearing surface prep
- Where debris or old lubricant is present, clean threads and bearing surfaces using non-abrasive brushes and compressed air per SB-1043. Dry surfaces before applying lubricant.
- Apply a light, even film of CFW-LUB-371 to threads and bearing surfaces where specified by equipment manufacturer or MM-P3-L4-HT02. Avoid over-application; excess lubricant can affect torque-to-tension relationship.

Torque verification
- Seat fasteners by hand to ensure correct engagement of threads. Use torque wrench to apply torque smoothly to achieve uniform clamp-up. If resistance indicates thread damage or binding, back out and re-clean; replace fastener only after documenting condition and approval per MM-P3-L4-HT02.
- When re-torquing assemblies that include load-sharing components (e.g., flange assemblies, door hardware), follow manufacturer pattern to achieve uniform compression and alignment. Record each fastener's identification and the applied tool used.
- If a fastener cannot be brought to the expected feel of a snug, documented attempt, do not force; stop, tag, and escalate to maintenance engineering per MM-P3-L4-HT02.

Examples and special cases
- Example: If a door hinge fastener exhibits fretting and surface pitting such that thread engagement is compromised, tag the fastener and replace with a torque-rated equivalent. Document the condition and replacement in the maintenance record and reference SB-1043 for corrosion mitigation guidance.
- Example: Fastener in proximity to quench manifold showing residue build-up—clean, apply CFW-LUB-371, and verify seating per procedure. Note any residue source in the record to support follow-up on quench system integrity.

Records to keep
- For each maintenance action on EQ-P3-L4-HT02, complete the fastener inspection log and attach the torque verification sheet. Record equipment id EQ-P3-L4-HT02, maintenance date, technician name, fastener location, condition observed, lubricant applied (CFW-LUB-371), and any tags placed.
- Maintain calibration proof for torque wrench used, referenced to SOP-P3-L4-01 records. File nonconformance tags and corrective action reports per MM-P3-L4-HT02.

Acceptance criteria
- All inspected fasteners must be free of thread damage that compromises engagement. Surface corrosion or fretting that reduces safe engagement requires replacement and documentation.
- All fasteners requiring lubricant must have a uniform film of CFW-LUB-371 applied where specified. Evidence of lubricant omission is cause for rework.
- Fasteners must seat and allow the technician to achieve a secure, repeatable clamp-up using calibrated torque tools. Any fastener that cannot be secured without thread damage or binding must be tagged, removed, or replaced and recorded.
- Maintenance records for EQ-P3-L4-HT02 must include completed inspection log, torque verification sheet, lubricant usage entry for CFW-LUB-371, and references to related document actions in MM-P3-L4-HT02, SB-1043, and SOP-P3-L4-01.

Notes on quench timing relevance
The quench delay maximum for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P3-L4-HT02) is 20 seconds. Fastener-related misalignment or leakage in quench manifolds can increase effective quench delay. Ensure fasteners on quench delivery assemblies are inspected and secured as part of this procedure to help maintain quench timing within acceptable process limits cited in MM-P3-L4-HT02.

Revision history
Rev F: Current content; supersedes Rev E. See MM-P3-L4-HT02 for prior revision trace and SB-1043 for corrosion handling guidance.

# MM-P3-L4-RR01 — Maintenance manual - Heat Treat radial ring rolling mill #1
Revision: Rev F (This revision supersedes Rev E)
Plant: P3, line P3-L4
Equipment: EQ-P3-L4-RR01

Scope
This document provides maintenance instructions, rationale, and acceptance criteria for the Heat Treat radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P3-L4-RR01) at Plant P3, line P3-L4. It is intended for trained maintenance engineers and technicians responsible for preventive maintenance, corrective repairs, and inspection activities on the mill. Related documents: SB-1028, SOP-P3-L4-02, SOP-P3-L4-03. Follow site lockout/tagout and hot-work procedures as directed in SOP-P3-L4-02 and SOP-P3-L4-03.

Background and purpose
The radial ring rolling mill at Heat Treat performs high-force deformation operations that rely on precise clamping and well-lubricated bearings. Failures in the mandrel clamp or main roll bearings can cause dimensional rejects, unexpected downtime, and safety hazards. This manual documents the essential maintenance tasks and the engineering rationale behind them, focusing on actions that influence part quality and machine reliability.

Key specification references
- The mandrel clamp bolt torque for Heat Treat radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P3-L4-RR01) is 605 N·m.
- The main roll bearing lubrication interval for Heat Treat radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P3-L4-RR01) is 135 hours.
These values are the controlling specifications for clamp integrity and bearing lubrication. Do not substitute alternative values without documented engineering approval referenced in SB-1028.

Tools
Recommended tools and consumables for tasks described below:
- Calibrated torque wrench sized to achieve specified mandrel clamp bolt torque
- Bearing grease gun compatible with bearing fittings
- Manufacturer-approved grease as specified in SB-1028
- Inspection mirror and strong portable light source
- Clean lint-free rags and approved solvent
- Fastener retention compound as specified in SB-1028
- Maintenance log forms and digital entry device for records
Only use tools that are calibrated and traceable per site calibration procedures. If replacement tools are used, record calibration status in maintenance records.

Procedure
General notes
- Perform all work with the mill fully de-energized and isolated per SOP-P3-L4-02. Verify isolation and document the verification.
- Use appropriate personal protective equipment and follow SOP-P3-L4-03 for hot surface and handling precautions.
- Clean work areas and components prior to inspection to avoid false indications.

Mandrel clamp bolt torque verification and adjustment
1. Prepare the clamp assembly by cleaning bolt threads and seating surfaces with approved solvent.
2. Inspect bolts and clamp components for wear or damage. If physical defects are present, remove the bolt and tag it for replacement per SB-1028.
3. Using the calibrated torque wrench, apply torque to each mandrel clamp bolt to the specified value: 605 N·m. Apply torque in a controlled manner and follow the clamp pattern to ensure even seating.
4. Where specified by SB-1028, apply fastener retention compound to the bolt threads after torque verification. Note: follow product cure guidance per SB-1028.
5. Record each bolt torque application in the maintenance log, including bolt identifier, operator initials, and any deviations.
Rationale: Controlled clamp torque ensures consistent mandrel seating and minimizes runout that can affect part geometry and bearing loads.

Main roll bearing lubrication
1. Verify bearing lubrication fittings are clean and free of contamination.
2. Using the approved grease and a properly primed grease gun, apply lubricant to each bearing fitting until slight purge of old lubricant is observed, or until bearing housing level indicates adequate fill as described in SB-1028.
3. Adhere to the controlling lubrication interval: The main roll bearing lubrication interval for Heat Treat radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P3-L4-RR01) is 135 hours. Record the timestamp of lubrication and the operating hours counter state in the maintenance log.
4. Inspect seals and housings for leaks during lubrication. If leaks are detected, tag the bearing assembly for repair and follow corrective procedures in SB-1028.
Rationale: Consistent lubrication reduces friction, heat, and wear, extending bearing life and maintaining dimensional stability of rolled rings.

Inspection and corrective actions
- Bearings: If abnormal noise, vibration, or leakage is observed, remove the bearing assembly for teardown and evaluation per SB-1028. Preserve bearing identification and condition photos for root cause analysis.
- Clamp bolts: Replace bolts that show thread damage, elongation, or surface defects. Use replacement parts and installation practices qualified in SB-1028.
- Records: Photograph critical conditions and attach to the corrective maintenance report.

Examples and scenarios
Example: If an operator reports increased roll vibration that coincides with torque verification showing a clamp bolt below specification, retorque all clamp bolts to 605 N·m and perform bearing lubrication. Log actions and monitor vibration per SOP-P3-L4-02. If vibration persists, escalate to engineering and initiate bearing inspection per SB-1028.
Example: During a routine lubrication, if heavy contamination is observed in the grease purge, sample the lubricant, note the contaminant description, and initiate bearing teardown and contamination analysis as specified in SB-1028.

Records to keep
Maintain the following records in the document control system and on the equipment maintenance history:
- Torque application log entries showing bolt identifiers, 605 N·m application confirmation, date, and technician initials.
- Lubrication entries documenting adherence to the 135 hours interval, grease type (as per SB-1028), amount applied, date, and technician initials.
- Inspection reports, photographs, and any nonconformance records generated during maintenance.
- Corrective action reports with root cause and disposition referencing SB-1028.

Acceptance criteria
The maintenance activity is acceptable when all of the following are met:
- Mandrel clamp bolts are torqued to the required value and show no physical defects or looseness after installation: 605 N·m applied and recorded.
- Main roll bearings have been serviced with the approved lubricant and the lubrication event is documented in accordance with the 135 hours interval.
- No abnormal noise, vibration, or leakage is present after return to service; if any abnormal condition remains, a documented corrective action and re-inspection plan must be in place per SB-1028.
- Maintenance records are complete and stored per SOP-P3-L4-02 and SOP-P3-L4-03.

References
SB-1028
SOP-P3-L4-02
SOP-P3-L4-03

# MM-P3-L4-RR01-S3 Calibration checks - Heat Treat radial ring rolling mill #1
Revision: Rev C (supersedes Rev B)  
Plant: P3, line P3-L4  
Equipment: EQ-P3-L4-RR01

Scope
This maintenance manual provides the calibration check procedure for Heat Treat radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P3-L4-RR01). It is limited to measurement, verification, and documentation tasks required to confirm that core sensing and positioning systems meet operational requirements for rings up to the maximum ring outer diameter for Heat Treat radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P3-L4-RR01) which is 2150 mm. Refer to SOP-P3-L4-02, SOP-P3-L4-03, and SOP-P3-L4-05 for start-up, lockout/tagout, and lubrication policies respectively.

Background
The radial ring rolling mill is a production-critical machine whose dimensional output is validated by a suite of sensors and encoders. Calibration checks ensure repeatable dimensional control and prevent off-spec forgings. This document covers checks for encoder linearity, radius and diameter measurement sensors, proximity switches used for home and limit detection, and general mechanical condition affecting measurement geometry. The lubricant part number for Heat Treat radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P3-L4-RR01) is CFW-LUB-315 and must be used per SOP-P3-L4-05 for all lubrication-related items noted in this procedure.

Tools
- Traceable gauge block set and ring master sized to near maximum working range up to 2150 mm.  
- Calibrated dial indicator or digital comparator with traceable calibration certificate.  
- Portable encoder reader compatible with installed encoder model.  
- Hand tools and non-marring alignment fixtures per SOP-P3-L4-02.  
- Clean rags and approved cleaner consistent with SOP-P3-L4-03.  
- Calibration record sheet and device certificates for attachment to the equipment maintenance file.

Procedure
Pre-checks
- Follow lockout/tagout and energy isolation as described in SOP-P3-L4-02 before any physical inspection or measurement. Ensure personnel carrying out checks are trained and authorized.
- Clean measurement surfaces, sensor windows, and target faces in accordance with SOP-P3-L4-03. Remove scale, grease, and debris to avoid false readings. Use only approved cleaners.

Mechanical alignment verification
- Position the tooling and carriage to a stable, accessible state following the machine vendor's safe handling guidance. Confirm that the anvil or reference face is clean and undamaged.
- Mount a ring master or reference ring near the centerline. Use the dial indicator to check runout at multiple radial positions around the reference ring. Use gentle contact to avoid deflection.
- If runout exceeds acceptable geometric indicators (documented in vendor records), flag the issue and initiate mechanical adjustment before proceeding to sensor checks. Record findings on the calibration record sheet.

Sensor and encoder checks
- With the reference ring in place, read the encoder outputs using the portable encoder reader. Compare encoder readings against the physical dimension measured with the dial indicator and the ring master. Note that the maximum ring outer diameter target in calculations is 2150 mm; verify that sensor outputs scale appropriately across the working range.
- Verify proximity switches at home and limits by slowly jogging the axis through the detection points and confirming consistent actuation. Clean and inspect switch targets and mounts for wear or misalignment.
- For linear position sensors, verify linearity by measuring at multiple positions across the range and comparing to the gauge block or ring master reference. Document each comparison on the calibration record.

Adjustment and verification
- If sensor readings are outside accepted deviation defined by the equipment vendor, adjust sensor mounting, offset values, or encoder indexing per manufacturer instructions and retest until within acceptable deviation. Note all adjustments with rationale and as-found/as-left values on the record sheet.
- After adjustments, perform a full sweep of the measurement range using the reference ring or master and record results to demonstrate repeatability.

Examples and rationale
- Example scenario: if encoder reading shows a consistent offset relative to the physical reference, a mechanical indexing error or electrical offset is indicated. Correction involves verifying encoder coupling, retorquing coupling hardware per vendor guidance, and updating encoder zero as needed. The rationale is that small mechanical misalignments translate directly into dimensional errors at the ring outer diameter, particularly near the specified maximum of 2150 mm.
- Example scenario: intermittent proximity switch actuation often results from contamination on the target face. Cleaning the face and verifying consistent actuation eliminates false home events that can cause positioning drift during a production cycle.

Acceptance criteria
- Calibration checks are acceptable when measured outputs from encoders and linear sensors show consistency with physical standards across the inspected positions and when proximity switches actuate reliably at their intended points. Measurements must demonstrate repeatability and correlation to the ring master reference with deviations within the equipment vendor’s permitted limits documented in the equipment file.
- Mechanical alignment is acceptable when runout and geometry checks do not introduce measurement bias across the usable range up to 2150 mm.
- Lubrication points addressed during the check must be serviced using lubricant part number CFW-LUB-315 as specified and recorded per SOP-P3-L4-05.

Records to keep
- Complete the calibration record sheet with as-found and as-left values, instrument calibration certificates, description of any adjustments, and the name and signature of the technician performing the check.
- Attach copies of relevant vendor tolerances, adjustment instructions, and any nonconformance reports raised as a result of the calibration check.
- Store records in the equipment maintenance file and reference them in the next scheduled review per plant document control practice.

Notes
- Follow the referenced SOPs for procedural controls: SOP-P3-L4-02 for safe isolation and SOP-P3-L4-03 for cleaning and handling, and SOP-P3-L4-05 for lubrication practices.
- Any deviation from acceptance criteria requires escalation to maintenance engineering and designation of corrective actions prior to returning EQ-P3-L4-RR01 to production.
title: Calibration checks - Heat Treat radial ring rolling mill #1

# QS-CFW-1140-78 Quality specification - axle hub CFW-1140-78 (4140)
Revision: Rev E  
Supersedes: Rev D  
Plant: P1  
Parts: CFW-1140-78

Scope
This quality specification defines acceptance criteria, inspection methods, and nonconformance handling for finished axle hub CFW-1140-78 (4140) produced at Plant P1. It applies to all production lots and to parts shipped as finished machined forgings under part designation CFW-1140-78. The intent is to ensure material and dimensional integrity consistent with service requirements while providing clear instructions for inspection personnel and quality engineers.

Background and rationale
CFW-1140-78 is a critical rotating component where hardness and bore control directly affect wear life and fit with mating bearings. The specified hardness range balances core toughness with surface wear resistance for the target application. Bore control is specified to ensure interference and alignment features assemble correctly. The maximum forging weight limits capacity and handling constraints in the P1 forging cell.

Requirements table
The following table lists the mandatory acceptance criteria for axle hub CFW-1140-78 (CFW-1140-78).

- Material: 4140 forging in condition per purchase drawing and process control records.
- The hardness range for axle hub CFW-1140-78 (CFW-1140-78) is 27-32 HRC.
- Bore diameter tolerance for axle hub CFW-1140-78 (CFW-1140-78) is ±0.08 mm.
- Maximum forging weight for axle hub CFW-1140-78 (CFW-1140-78) is 74.6 kg.
- Surface finish, thread, and secondary machining features to be verified against the released engineering drawing at final inspection.
- No visible forging discontinuities that would jeopardize structural integrity allowed; examples include through-thickness laps or unblended laps at critical fillets.

Inspection method
General approach
Inspectors shall verify conformance to the Requirements table using calibrated methods traceable to the quality system. Use controlled gaging and calibrated hardness equipment operated by qualified personnel. Record results in the inspection record specified below.

Hardness
Measure hardness at locations representative of the functional surface and cross section. Ensure surface preparation consistent with the hardness instrument manufacturer's guidance and the quality laboratory procedures. Record each reading and the measurement location. Compare results directly to the requirement.

Bore diameter
Measure the bore using appropriate metrology equipment capable of resolving the tolerance band defined above. Measure at positions representative of the bearing mount and at circumferentially separated locations to detect out-of-round conditions. Use contact or non-contact methods validated for the bore geometry. Report the nominal value and the deviation relative to the requirement.

Weight and visual
Verify forging weight by scale at receipt from the forging operation; if scale records are digital, ensure they are stamped into the lot record. Perform a visual inspection for forgings, focusing on flash removal, gating remnants, and fillet blending. Record any deviations.

Examples of acceptable and rejectable findings
- Example acceptable: Hardness readings within the specified range taken at multiple representative locations; bore measurements consistent across locations within the specified tolerance band; forging weight below the maximum forging weight value.
- Example rejectable: Hardness readings outside the specified range at any representative location; bore measurement exceeding the specified tolerance in any measured location; forging weight over the stated maximum forging weight value.

Calibration and equipment
All measuring devices used for hardness, dimensional measurement, and weighing shall be calibrated per the laboratory control plan and have current calibration status documented in the instrument log. Operators shall be certified to perform the measurement techniques required for this part.

Records to keep
Maintain the following records as part of the lot quality package:
- Incoming forging inspection record with hardness readings and instrument identification.
- Dimensional inspection report with raw measurements, probe/fixture identification, and measurement locations.
- Scale weight record showing the measured forging weight and the operator name.
- Nonconformance records and disposition documentation when any requirement is not met.
- Calibration certificates for instruments used during inspection for traceability.

Nonconformance handling
When a part or lot fails to meet any requirement in this specification, follow the nonconformance handling process below.

Containment
Segregate affected material from conforming material to prevent inadvertent use. Tag material with a nonconforming status indicator and record lot identifiers in the nonconformance log.

Evaluation
Quality shall perform an evaluation to determine the extent of nonconformance and potential impact on downstream processes and customers. For dimensional deviations, use actual measured data to assess whether machining or rework can restore conformance without compromising critical features. For hardness deviations, consult metallurgical resources to assess whether heat treatment or blending options are permissible under engineering change control.

Disposition
Acceptable dispositions include rework to drawing requirements, use-as-is with documented engineering approval, or scrap. All dispositions must be documented in the nonconformance record with justification and authorized signatures. If rework or heat treatment is authorized, specify controls to prevent recurrence and document subsequent verification inspections.

Examples of disposition scenarios
- Example disposition: A single bore measurement marginally out of tolerance may be eligible for machining to drawing controls when engineering documents a allowable corrective action and the action is recorded in the lot file.
- Example disposition: Hardness values outside the specified range require metallurgical evaluation and documented approval before any use-as-is disposition.

Records of disposition and root cause
Keep the nonconformance report, root cause analysis, corrective actions, and verification results within the lot file. Track trends for recurring issues and initiate process improvement actions where patterns are identified.

Responsibilities
Production is responsible for producing forgings to controlled process standards. Quality is responsible for acceptance sampling, maintaining inspection records, and initiating nonconformance processing. Metallurgy is responsible for evaluating material condition deviations and recommending corrective actions.

Appendix
Inspection forms and templates referenced in this specification are maintained within the P1 document control system and linked to the part family under company records. Ensure the lot quality package accompanies shipments of CFW-1140-78 when required by customer contract or internal shipping procedures.
