# QS-CFW-1159-60 — Quality specification - track link CFW-1159-60 (15B37)
Revision: Rev F  
Plant: P3  
Parts: CFW-1159-60  
This revision supersedes Rev E.

Scope
- This quality specification applies to forged track link CFW-1159-60 (CFW-1159-60) produced at Plant P3. It defines acceptance criteria, inspection methods, and handling of nonconforming material for production, heat treatment, machining, and final inspection operations associated with the part family identified above. The scope includes forged blanks, finished machined links, and assembled link sets delivered under the CFW-1159-60 part identifier.

Background and rationale
- Track link CFW-1159-60 (CFW-1159-60) is a high-wear component used in undercarriage systems. The functional life of the component depends on controlled hardness, accurate bore geometry, and adherence to forging weight limits to ensure proper material flow during forming and consistent heat treatment response. The hardness range is set to balance wear resistance with fracture toughness for application conditions. Bore tolerance controls press-fit and pin retention; the specified forging weight limit ensures die life and consistent microstructure in the finished part. These parameters were selected based on historical production data and laboratory correlation of hardness to fatigue performance.

Requirements table
- Material and identification
  - Material shall be as specified on the purchase order for parts CFW-1159-60. Each delivered part shall be legibly marked or tagged with the part identifier CFW-1159-60 and the heat lot or batch code associated with the melt.

- Hardness
  - The hardness range for track link CFW-1159-60 (CFW-1159-60) is 36-40 HRC.

- Bore diameter
  - The bore diameter tolerance for track link CFW-1159-60 (CFW-1159-60) is ±0.01 mm.

- Forging weight
  - The maximum forging weight for track link CFW-1159-60 (CFW-1159-60) is 80.0 kg.

- Surface condition and discontinuities
  - Forgings shall be free of visible forging laps, through-thickness cracks, and other discontinuities that would compromise service performance. Light mill scale and minor surface oxide permitted if removed prior to final inspection.

- Documentation and traceability
  - Each batch shall be accompanied by manufacturing records showing heat lot, forging operation reference, heat-treatment record, and final inspection sign-off.

Inspection method
- Overview
  - Inspections are performed at incoming material receipt, post-forging, post-heat-treatment, post-machining, and final inspection before shipment. Critical characteristics listed in the requirements table shall be verified by qualified personnel using calibrated equipment traceable to internal calibration records.

- Hardness measurement procedure
  - Perform hardness readings on the machined or heat-treated surface at locations representative of the high-wear regions and the web near the bore. Use an appropriate Rockwell hardness tester calibrated per internal calibration practice. Take multiple readings across the component to account for local variation. Record individual readings and calculate the observed range. Parts outside the stated hardness range shall be identified as nonconforming.

- Bore diameter measurement procedure
  - Inspect bore diameter using a calibrated bore gauge or coordinate measuring equipment capable of resolving the stated tolerance. Measure at several axial positions and at orthogonal angles to detect out-of-round conditions. Record nominal values and deviations. Accept only those parts where all measured bore diameters fall within the tolerance band defined in the requirements table.

- Forging weight verification
  - Verify forging weight at the forging operation by weighing the blank after trimming and prior to heat treatment. Ensure each blank does not exceed the maximum forging weight specified in the requirements table. Record the measured weight on the forging route card.

- Sampling and frequency
  - Selectivity for sampling shall be aligned with process capability and risk assessment. For routine production, include hardness and bore checks on every lot prior to machining and on finished parts. For low-volume or prototype runs, increase inspection coverage as required by engineering.

- Calibration and equipment
  - Use calibrated instruments for hardness, dimensional, and mass measurements. Record calibration references and due dates in the inspection record.

Nonconformance handling
- Identification and segregation
  - Any part or lot found outside the specified requirements shall be tagged as nonconforming and segregated from conforming stock. Marking shall include part identifier, lot code, and the nature of the nonconformance.

- Evaluation and disposition
  - Engineering shall evaluate nonconforming items to determine root cause and disposition. Disposition options include rework, repair, use-as-is with concession, or scrap. For hardness out-of-specification items, evaluate potential reheat or reprocessing only after metallurgical assessment confirms rework will restore required properties without introducing detrimental effects. For bore tolerance issues, evaluate whether machining corrections are feasible without impacting part geometry or function.

- Example dispositions
  - Example: A lot exhibiting hardness below the specified range may be held for microstructural analysis; if analysis shows incomplete transformation, reheat and controlled quench may be authorized by engineering with documented parameters and subsequent verification to the hardness criteria. Example: A bore slightly oversize beyond tolerance may be rejected for service use and either scrapped or returned to vendor if outside repair capability.

- Root cause and corrective action
  - Initiate formal corrective action when nonconformance indicates process drift or recurring defects. Document root cause, containment actions, corrective actions, and verify effectiveness through follow-up inspections and trend data.

Records to keep
- Maintain the following records with the lot history for each production batch of CFW-1159-60:
  - Forging route card with measured forging weight and operator sign-off.
  - Heat-treatment records tied to the heat lot.
  - Hardness test records showing individual readings and location notation.
  - Dimensional inspection reports including bore measurements and instrument identification.
  - Nonconformance reports and disposition documentation.
  - Final inspection sign-off and packing release.

Retention
- Inspection and traceability records shall be retained in the document control system per Plant P3 record retention practice and made available for customer review upon request.

Notes
- This specification is the controlling quality requirement for CFW-1159-60 at Plant P3. Any deviation from the requirements above must be authorized in writing by engineering and documented on the lot record prior to shipment.

# QS-CFW-1392-34 — Quality specification - crankshaft blank CFW-1392-34 (4340)
Revision: Rev E  
This revision supersedes Rev D.  
Plant: P1  
Parts: CFW-1392-34

Scope
This quality specification defines acceptance requirements, inspection methods, and nonconformance handling for crankshaft blank CFW-1392-34 (CFW-1392-34) manufactured from 4340 material at Plant P1. The intent is to ensure blanks meet metallurgical and dimensional targets necessary for downstream machining and heat treatment operations. Applicable to all production and repair forgings identified as crankshaft blank CFW-1392-34 (CFW-1392-34) produced under this part number at Plant P1.

Requirements table
The table below lists controlled characteristics and the required limits that must be verified prior to release of crankshaft blank CFW-1392-34 (CFW-1392-34) from the forging cell.

- Characteristic: Hardness — Requirement: The hardness range for crankshaft blank CFW-1392-34 (CFW-1392-34) is 34-37 HRC.
- Characteristic: Bore diameter tolerance — Requirement: The bore diameter tolerance for crankshaft blank CFW-1392-34 (CFW-1392-34) is ±0.04 mm.
- Characteristic: Maximum forging weight — Requirement: The maximum forging weight for crankshaft blank CFW-1392-34 (CFW-1392-34) is 6.7 kg.

Notes on requirements
- Hardness is a metallurgical acceptance criterion intended to confirm correct forging and cooling practice for the 4340 chemistry and to prevent excessive distortion or cracking during subsequent processes.
- Bore diameter tolerance is defined to ensure interchangeability and to minimize rework during finish machining.
- Maximum forging weight controls material usage and ensures compatibility with material handling and die capacity.

Inspection method
General approach
Inspectors must verify each characteristic listed in the requirements table prior to release of the batch or individual part as defined by production routing. Inspections must be documented on the part inspection record and retained as described in the Records section below.

Hardness
Measure hardness on each representative crankshaft blank CFW-1392-34 (CFW-1392-34) in a location free of scale and surface deformation, perpendicular to the bore axis and in an area that will not be removed during normal machining. Report the measured hardness and verify it falls within the specified range: 34-37 HRC. If surface preparation is required to obtain valid readings, document the prep method.

Bore diameter
Verify bore diameter using calibrated gauges or measurement instruments capable of achieving resolution and accuracy consistent with the specified bore diameter tolerance: ±0.04 mm. Record the measured bore diameter against the nominal dimension on the inspection record and state whether it is within tolerance.

Weight
Confirm forging weight does not exceed the maximum forging weight for crankshaft blank CFW-1392-34 (CFW-1392-34) is 6.7 kg. Use calibrated scales and record the measured weight on the inspection record.

Traceability and evidence
For each inspection, record:
- Part identifier: CFW-1392-34
- Plant: P1
- Inspector name or identifier
- Measurement tool identification and calibration status
- Actual measurement values for hardness, bore, and weight
- A pass/fail statement for each characteristic and overall disposition

Examples
- Example acceptance: A crankshaft blank CFW-1392-34 (CFW-1392-34) measured at 35 HRC, bore diameter recorded within ±0.04 mm, and weight at or below 6.7 kg is acceptable for release.
- Example rejection: A crankshaft blank CFW-1392-34 (CFW-1392-34) measured at 33 HRC or 38 HRC, a bore outside ±0.04 mm of nominal, or weight above 6.7 kg is nonconforming and must follow the Nonconformance Handling procedure.

Nonconformance handling
Identification
Any part that fails to meet any requirement in the Requirements table must be clearly identified as nonconforming and segregated from conforming material to prevent unintended use.

Containment
Segregate the nonconforming crankshaft blank CFW-1392-34 (CFW-1392-34) and attach a nonconformance tag that includes part identifier, plant, inspector, measured values, and reason for rejection as recorded on the inspection record.

Disposition options
Disposition may include rework if the defect is repairable to meet the specified requirements, return to scrap, or use-as-is only if approved through the formal engineering deviation process. Engineering deviation requests must include supporting inspection data and a justification demonstrating no adverse effect on function, safety, or downstream processes.

Engineering review
When rework or deviation is proposed, submit the inspection record and proposed corrective action to engineering for review. Engineering will evaluate the metallurgical and dimensional implications and authorize disposition in writing if acceptable.

Root cause and corrective action
For repeated occurrences of the same nonconformance, implement root cause analysis and corrective actions. Document findings, corrective steps taken, and verification activities demonstrating the issue is addressed.

Records to keep
Maintain inspection records, nonconformance tags, weighing records, and calibration certificates for all measurement instruments used. Records must include the data elements described in the Traceability and evidence section and must be retained in the document control system associated with QS-CFW-1392-34. Records should be sufficient to recreate inspection decisions and to support any future engineering reviews or audits.

Revision control
This document is Revision Rev E and supersedes the previous revision Rev D. All changes from Rev D are captured in the revision history maintained in the document control system.

End of specification.

# QS-CFW-1466-55 — Quality specification - bearing ring CFW-1466-55 (52100)
Revision: Rev C  
Plant: P2  
Parts: CFW-1466-55  
This revision supersedes Rev B.

Scope
This quality specification defines acceptance criteria, inspection methods, and nonconformance handling for bearing ring CFW-1466-55 (CFW-1466-55), material 52100, manufactured at Plant P2. It applies to all production forgings, machining, heat treatment, and final inspection activities for the part number CFW-1466-55 processed under Cascade Forge Works procedural controls. The intent is to ensure dimensional integrity, metallurgical performance, and documented traceability prior to release to supplied parts inventory.

Requirements table
The following table lists the controlled attributes, required values, and applicable acceptance notes.

| Attribute | Requirement | Acceptance notes |
|---|---:|---|
| Hardness (bearing ring CFW-1466-55) | 36-41 HRC. | Measure on raceway and cross section after final heat treatment. Readings outside the range are cause for nonconformance handling. |
| Bore diameter tolerance (bearing ring CFW-1466-55) | ±0.03 mm. | Tolerance applies to final machined bore diameter. Use calibrated bore gauges; record actual diameter in inspection record. |
| Maximum forging weight (bearing ring CFW-1466-55) | 27.4 kg. | Maximum weight applies to individual forging blank prior to machining. Exceeding weight may trigger scrap or rework disposition per nonconformance handling. |

Inspection method
Background and rationale
These inspection methods are selected to verify that mechanical hardness and dimensional tolerances meet design intent for rolling element interface and assembly fit. Hardness band is chosen to balance wear resistance and toughness for 52100 in this application. Bore tolerance is controlled to ensure press fit and bearing clearance after assembly. Maximum forging weight is controlled to ensure material homogeneity, quench performance, and machine handling compatibility with Plant P2 equipment.

General procedure
- Preparation: Identify the part as CFW-1466-55 and verify material certification. Ensure part is cleaned of machining oils and particulate that could affect measurements.
- Equipment: Use hardness tester capable of Rockwell C scale calibrated per plant calibration procedure. Use bore gauges and micrometers calibrated per plant calibration procedure. Use scales and handling equipment rated for the part mass limits of Plant P2.
- Measurement locations: For hardness, test on the raceway surface and at a representative cross section at the midpoint of the ring wall. For bore diameter, measure at multiple circumferential locations to detect out-of-roundness; report the maximum deviation and the measured mean diameter.
- Recording: Document each measured attribute on the inspection record for CFW-1466-55. For hardness, record each reading and the average if multiple readings are taken. For bore diameter, record each measurement and the measured diameter reported against the tolerance ±0.03 mm. For forging weight, record the measured blank weight on the heat treatment and process traveler.

Examples and interpretation
- If hardness readings on the raceway are 36-41 HRC., the part meets the hardness requirement. If any reading is below 36 HRC. or above 41 HRC., treat as nonconforming.
- If bore measurements remain within ±0.03 mm. of the nominal dimension and show acceptable geometric form, the part meets the bore requirement. If any measurement falls outside ±0.03 mm., follow nonconformance handling.
- If a forging blank is measured at a mass that exceeds 27.4 kg., the blank exceeds the maximum forging weight requirement; initiate disposition actions per nonconformance handling.

Sample sizes and frequency
Inspection is required on each final lot of CFW-1466-55 parts prior to release. The inspection record shall demonstrate that the attributes listed in the requirements table were verified for representative pieces and package lots in accordance with Plant P2 standard sampling logic. All critical characteristic measurements shall be traceable to the lot or heat number.

Calibration and traceability
All measurement equipment used for verification of the specified attributes must be calibrated and traceable to the Plant P2 calibration system. Maintain calibration certificates with the inspection records for each instrument used.

Records to keep
- Final inspection record for CFW-1466-55 showing hardness readings, bore measurements, and forging weight entry for the lot.
- Material certification for the 52100 heat batch associated with each lot of parts.
- Equipment calibration certificates for hardness tester, bore gauges, and scales used in inspection.
- Disposition records for any nonconforming material processed under nonconformance handling.

Nonconformance handling
Identification and segregation
Parts that fail any requirement in the requirements table shall be identified as nonconforming and segregated from conforming inventory immediately. Use the Plant P2 nonconforming tag and place parts in the designated nonconformance area to prevent unintended use.

Disposition options
- Rework: If the nonconformance is dimensional and rework will reliably restore the attribute within specification without adversely affecting material properties, document the proposed rework and obtain authorization from Quality Engineering. Reworked parts must undergo full verification per the inspection method and be recorded.
- Repair by machining is not permitted if it would compromise the controlled hardness range 36-41 HRC. or if it requires removal of heat-affected material that would change mechanical properties.
- Scrap: If the part cannot be returned to specification by approved rework, disposition as scrap is mandatory. Document scrap reason and material flow to scrap processing.
- Return to supplier: If the root cause is linked to incoming material or a forging process outside Plant P2 responsibility, document the evidence and coordinate return or credit action with the supplier.

Root cause and corrective action
For any nonconformance, perform root cause analysis using the Plant P2 corrective action process. Document findings, containment measures, and corrective/preventive actions. Update process controls where necessary to prevent recurrence.

Closure and record retention
Quality Engineering must approve final disposition and sign off on completed corrective actions. Retain inspection, disposition, and corrective action records for CFW-1466-55 in the document control system as applicable to Plant P2 retention policy.

# QS-CFW-1476-90 Quality specification - connecting rod CFW-1476-90 (1045)
Revision: Rev F — This revision supersedes Rev E  
Plant: P3  
Parts: CFW-1476-90

Scope
This quality specification defines material, dimensional, hardness, weight, inspection, and disposition requirements for connecting rod CFW-1476-90 manufactured at Plant P3. It applies to all forged and finish-machined parts produced to part identification CFW-1476-90 and to associated incoming raw forgings supplied for processing under Cascade Forge Works manufacturing control. The intent is to provide clear acceptance criteria, inspection methods, and nonconformance handling so that manufacturing, quality, and receiving personnel have a single source of requirements for this part.

Background and rationale
The connecting rod is a safety-critical rotating assembly component. Control of hardness in the rod body, control of bore geometry, and limiting forging mass are necessary to assure mechanical performance and to manage downstream machining and assembly processes. The specified hardness range is chosen to balance fatigue resistance with machinability for the nominal alloy. The bore diameter tolerance is specified to ensure bearing fit and consistent assembly clearance. The maximum forging weight limits furnace load, die life, and handling constraints in Plant P3.

Requirements table

| Characteristic | Requirement | Inspection reference |
|---|---:|---|
| Material | Meet supplied alloy and heat treatment per purchase order and process sheet for CFW-1476-90 | Process sheet |
| Hardness (rod body) | 35-39 HRC | See Inspection method |
| Bore diameter tolerance | ±0.02 mm | See Inspection method |
| Maximum forging weight | 41.6 kg | Receiving and handling |

Notes for table:
- Hardness applies to the forged and heat-treated rod body after any specified tempering or stabilization operations and before final machining operations that may alter surface hardness. If surface treatments are applied that change surface hardness, report both surface and core results per Inspection method.
- Bore diameter tolerance applies to final machined bearing bore dimensions measured in accordance with the Inspection method. Where fitup with mating bearings is affected, use the tolerance above as the primary acceptance criterion.
- Maximum forging weight applies to the raw forging state as received from the drop forge or upset forge operation. Do not accept forgings that exceed the stated maximum forging weight.

Inspection method
General principles
Inspection shall be performed by qualified personnel in a controlled environment. Calibrated instruments shall be used, with calibration traceable to national standards. Record measurements in the part inspection record associated with the specific heat lot and process lot.

Hardness
- Hardness measurements shall be made on the cross section of the rod body at locations representative of the bulk material, avoiding surface-affected zones and machined surfaces. Use a hardness tester appropriate for the alloy and the target range.
- Record each result in the inspection record and report the measured value for each test location. Acceptance requires that reported values for representative locations fall within 35-39 HRC. When a measurement falls outside the range, follow Nonconformance handling.
- For confirmation of through-thickness hardness, perform a minimum of three representative indentations at different radial positions and report individual results in the inspection record.

Bore diameter
- Measure bearing bores using inside micrometers, bore gauges, or coordinate measurement equipment suitable to the tolerance class. Measurement must be performed in a fixture that adequately constrains the part to eliminate distortion during measurement.
- Record the nominal diameter and deviation from nominal. The acceptance criterion is ±0.02 mm relative to the drawing nominal. If any measured bore exceeds the tolerance band, the part is nonconforming.
- For assemblies where concentricity or runout impacts function, report all related measurements in the inspection record for traceability.

Forging weight
- Weigh incoming forgings on calibrated scales. Record the forging weight on the receiving inspection report.
- Accept incoming forgings only if the measured forging weight does not exceed 41.6 kg. For forgings below that value, proceed with normal processing and document the measured weight.

Examples and typical records to keep
- Part inspection record: For each inspected part, include part identifier CFW-1476-90, heat lot, process lot, inspector name, instrument IDs, hardness readings with locations, bore measurements with method and instrument, forging weight, and disposition decision. Store records in the document control system under the corresponding lot folder.
- Receiving inspection report: For each forging receipt, include supplier identifier, gross forging weight entry, visual acceptance, and any immediate nonconformances observed. Attach weight verification showing 41.6 kg limit compliance.
- Calibration records: Maintain calibration certificates for hardness tester, bore measurement tools, and scale. Link the calibration record IDs to the inspection records for traceability.
- Deviation log: When a part is dispositioned as nonconforming, record details in the nonconformance log with references to corrective actions and final disposition.

Nonconformance handling
Identification and segregation
- Any part that fails to meet the hardness requirement of 35-39 HRC, that has bore measurements outside ±0.02 mm, or any incoming forging that exceeds 41.6 kg is nonconforming.
- Immediately tag and segregate nonconforming parts to prevent inadvertent use. Mark tags with part id CFW-1476-90 and reference the inspection record.

Investigation and disposition
- Perform a root cause review for each nonconformance. Record findings and recommended corrective actions in the nonconformance report.
- Possible dispositions include rework where feasible, use-as-is under engineering approval, or scrap. Rework that would change the metallurgical state or final dimensions must be approved by engineering and documented.
- Engineering approval for any concession must be recorded in the part inspection record and crossed-referenced in the nonconformance log.

Records retention
- Retain inspection records, receiving reports, calibration certificates, and nonconformance records in accordance with Plant P3 document retention policy and the Cascade Forge Works quality management system. Ensure traceability from finished part back to forging and heat lot.

This specification is controlled. Any departure from the requirements herein requires documented engineering approval and updating of the process documentation for CFW-1476-90.

# QS-CFW-1730-97 — Quality specification - valve body CFW-1730-97 (F316)
Revision: Rev B  
Plant: P2  
Parts: CFW-1730-97  
This revision supersedes Rev A.

Scope
This quality specification defines mandatory acceptance criteria and inspection practices for valve body CFW-1730-97 (CFW-1730-97) forged from material F316 at Plant P2. It applies to all production, repair, and returned material where the part is identified by the part designation above. The objective is to ensure dimensional accuracy, mechanical properties, and traceable disposition of nonconforming items prior to release to machining or shipping.

Requirements table
The table below lists the required attributes, acceptance criteria, and the primary record to be retained for each attribute.

- Attribute: Material identification  
  Acceptance criteria: Material lot and heat code must match certification from melt source and be recorded on the material receipt record.  
  Record: Material receipt and heat traceability record.

- Attribute: Hardness  
  Acceptance criteria: The hardness range for valve body CFW-1730-97 (CFW-1730-97) is 27-33 HRC. Hardness measurements shall be representative of the forging and performed on machined reference coupons or on specified locations when coupons are not available.  
  Record: Hardness log with location notation and operator initials.

- Attribute: Critical bore diameter  
  Acceptance criteria: The bore diameter tolerance for valve body CFW-1730-97 (CFW-1730-97) is ±0.09 mm from nominal drawing dimension. Measurement shall be taken after rough machining to the control plane specified by engineering, and again after final finish as part of final inspection.  
  Record: Dimensional inspection report with bore measurement entries and serial or batch identifiers.

- Attribute: Forging mass  
  Acceptance criteria: The maximum forging weight for valve body CFW-1730-97 (CFW-1730-97) is 148.1 kg. All forgings must be weighed and the mass recorded; forgings exceeding this mass must be segregated and dispositioned by engineering.  
  Record: Weighing log with operator initials and material linkage.

- Attribute: Visual and surface condition  
  Acceptance criteria: No cracks, laps, or forge defects that compromise machinability or mechanical integrity. Surface conditions that require additional machining shall be noted and approved by process engineering.  
  Record: Visual inspection checklist and photo record when defects are noted.

Inspection method
The following inspection practices define methods, rationale, and records to be maintained for verification of the requirements listed above.

- Hardness testing method and rationale  
  Use a Rockwell hardness tester calibrated to laboratory standards. Test locations should be selected to represent the thinnest and thickest cross sections and any heat-affected zones as identified by the forging operation. If a production coupon is available from the same heat and process, hardness may be performed on the coupon in lieu of direct part testing provided traceability to the forging batch is maintained. Record each test entry with part or coupon identifier, test location description, tester initials, and date.

- Bore diameter measurement method and rationale  
  Bore diameter shall be measured using calibrated bore gauges or coordinate measuring equipment. Measurement must reference the drawing nominal and apply the tolerance as specified: the bore diameter tolerance for valve body CFW-1730-97 (CFW-1730-97) is ±0.09 mm. Rationale: maintaining this tolerance ensures sealing surfaces and mating components assemble without excessive interference or leakage risk. Report actual measured values on the dimensional inspection report. When multiple bores or positions are present, record all measured locations with identifiers.

- Mass verification method and rationale  
  Weigh each forging on calibrated scales that are certified per plant practice. The maximum forging weight for valve body CFW-1730-97 (CFW-1730-97) is 148.1 kg; this is used to confirm correct material removal allowances, fixture capacities, and handling equipment selection. Record the measured mass and reconcile with expected forging mass based on engineering documentation.

- Visual inspection and surface evaluation method and rationale  
  Inspect under consistent lighting and, where practical, magnification for surface defects. Record visual findings on the visual inspection checklist. Photograph any condition that requires engineering disposition and attach to the inspection record. For defects that may be subsurface, escalate to non-destructive examination per nonconformance handling.

Records to keep
Maintain the following records in the document control system for each lot or part processed:

- Material receipt and heat traceability record.  
- Hardness log.  
- Dimensional inspection report including bore measurements.  
- Weighing log showing the recorded mass.

Example: If bore diameter is outside the bore diameter tolerance for valve body CFW-1730-97 (CFW-1730-97) is ±0.09 mm due to excess material, controlled machining to nominal may be acceptable if sufficient stock exists and material integrity is assured. All corrective actions must be recorded and authorized on the disposition record.

- Records of nonconformance

Attach any rework records and final inspection verification to the nonconformance report.

This revision supersedes Rev D.

Scope
- This quality specification applies to the manufacture, inspection, and disposition of flange blank CFW-3043-62 (4140) produced at Plant P1 for the part CFW-3043-62.
- It defines acceptance criteria, inspection methods, and nonconformance handling for material, forging, and finished blank characteristics necessary to meet downstream machining and assembly requirements.
- The document is mandatory for production, quality, and receiving inspection functions responsible for this part.

Requirements table
- Material
  - Material grade: 4140 per applicable purchase specification for steel forgings.
  - Certification: Mill test report required to accompany each heat batch and retained in the lot record.

- Mechanical
  - Hardness: The hardness range for flange blank CFW-3043-62 (CFW-3043-62) is 37-43 HRC.
  - Maximum forging weight: The maximum forging weight for flange blank CFW-3043-62 (CFW-3043-62) is 28.1 kg.

- Dimensional
  - Bore diameter tolerance: The bore diameter tolerance for flange blank CFW-3043-62 (CFW-3043-62) is ±0.03 mm.
  - Critical dimensions: All critical dimensions listed on the released print shall be verified in accordance with the inspection method section.

- Surface condition and defects
  - Forgings shall be free from laps, folds, forge laps, internal cracks, and other discontinuities that would compromise safe machining or cause rejection per visual and NDT criteria defined below.

Inspection method
- Sampling and lot definition
  - A lot is defined as all flange blanks produced from a single forging heat and single die set run. Inspection shall be performed on the lot and recorded in the lot inspection record.
- Visual inspection
  - Performed at receiving and post-forge stages. Inspect for surface discontinuities, scale, and forging defects. Use direct visual examination under adequate lighting and magnification appropriate for detecting the types of discontinuities shown on the drawing.
  - Examples of rejectable defects: continuous surface cracks that penetrate the machined surface envelope; prominent laps that cannot be removed by standard cleaning without reducing required metal allowances; evidence of internal separation visible at the surface after straightening or finishing.
- Dimensional inspection
  - Bore diameter: Measure bore diameter using a calibrated bore gauge or equivalent. Measurement shall be recorded to show compliance with the specified tolerance. The bore diameter tolerance for flange blank CFW-3043-62 (CFW-3043-62) is ±0.03 mm.
  - All measurements must be taken after any heat treatment or stress relief operations that are specified for the blank prior to machining, and recorded on the lot inspection record.
- Hardness testing
  - Verify hardness using a calibrated hardness tester capable of producing Rockwell C scale readings and following standard hardness test practice. Readings shall be taken at locations representative of the cross section, avoiding surface work-hardened zones and machining marks.
  - Acceptance: The hardness range for flange blank CFW-3043-62 (CFW-3043-62) is 37-43 HRC.
  - Record test locations, individual readings, and average values on the lot inspection record. If hardness readings fall outside the specified range, follow nonconformance handling.
- Weight verification
  - Confirm forging weight against the work order. The maximum forging weight for flange blank CFW-3043-62 (CFW-3043-62) is 28.1 kg. Record actual weight on the lot record.
- Nondestructive testing
  - Where indicated on the drawing or by process control, perform applicable surface or volumetric NDT. The specific NDT method and acceptance criteria are those called out on the product drawing and process routing.

Rationale and step detail
- Hardness rationale
  - The specified hardness range balances machinability and in-service strength for 4140 steel in this application. Values below the lower limit may indicate inadequate heat treatment, risking reduced wear resistance. Values above the upper limit may indicate over-hardening, increasing brittleness and machining difficulty. Hardness confirmation prior to machining reduces scrap and downstream rework.
- Bore tolerance rationale
  - The tight bore diameter tolerance ensures fit-up with mating components and minimizes machining allowance. Measuring the bore at final forging stage prevents acceptance of parts that will require excessive machining or rework.
- Weight control rationale
  - The maximum forging weight protects die and press capacity and ensures safe handling throughout the process flow. Verification prevents overload conditions and maintains consistent material usage.

Examples
- Example acceptable condition: A blank shows a smooth fillet transition, no visible laps, bore measured within the bore diameter tolerance, hardness within the specified range, and weight below the maximum forging weight. The lot inspection record is completed and the lot is released to machining.
- Example reject condition: A blank with subsurface separation exposed after light dressing, hardness above the specified range, or bore outside the specified tolerance shall be segregated and processed per the nonconformance handling section.

Nonconformance handling
- Segregation and identification
  - Nonconforming items shall be physically segregated and labeled to prevent unintended use. The lot inspection record shall flag the lot as nonconforming and include the reason for rejection.
- Disposition options
  - Rework: If the defect is remediable within the drawing allowances and without violating other specifications, an authorized disposition may allow rework. Reworked items must be reinspected and records updated.
  - Use as is: Only permitted with documented approval from authorized quality and engineering, and when the deviation does not affect form, fit, or function.
  - Scrap: Items that cannot be safely reworked or that compromise integrity shall be scrapped and recorded.
- Records and approvals
  - For every nonconformance, document the defect description, inspection data that led to the nonconformance determination, proposed disposition, and approvals. Retain these records in the lot file.
  - Corrective action follow-up: For recurring issues, generate a corrective action record referencing the lot identification and summarizing root cause analysis and corrective measures.

Records to keep
- Lot inspection record including mill test report, visual inspection notes, dimensional measurements (including bore diameter with the specified tolerance), hardness test results (showing compliance with the specified hardness range), and weight verification (showing compliance with maximum forging weight).
- Nonconformance records, dispositions, and approvals.
- Calibration certificates for inspection equipment used for this part.

# QS-CFW-3173-95 — Quality specification - gear blank CFW-3173-95 (8620)
Revision: Rev E  
Supersedes: Rev D  
Plant: P1  
Parts: CFW-3173-95

Scope
This quality specification establishes the acceptance requirements, inspection methods, and nonconformance handling for gear blank CFW-3173-95 (CFW-3173-95), manufactured from material grade 8620, for use in forged gear applications produced at Plant P1. It applies to all production lots, including first article and routine production, and covers dimensional, hardness, and mass limits that define acceptability at final forging prior to downstream heat treat or machining operations. This document is the controlling specification for inspection personnel, quality engineers, receiving inspection, and production supervisors for this part.

Requirements table
The table below lists the mandatory acceptance criteria for gear blank CFW-3173-95 (CFW-3173-95). Each line is a controlled characteristic to be recorded on inspection documentation.

| Characteristic | Requirement | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| Hardness, as-forged | The hardness range for gear blank CFW-3173-95 (CFW-3173-95) is 37-43 HRC. | Measure on representative surfaces; avoid scale and heavy decarb zones. |
| Bore diameter | The bore diameter tolerance for gear blank CFW-3173-95 (CFW-3173-95) is ±0.03 mm. | Inspect after finish boring where applicable; report deviation from nominal. |
| Mass | The maximum forging weight for gear blank CFW-3173-95 (CFW-3173-95) is 125.8 kg. | Weigh prior to batching for heat treatment; note net casting/forging weight. |

Inspection method
General approach
Inspection shall be performed by qualified inspectors using calibrated instruments and documented procedures. All inspection activities shall be performed in a controlled area free of heavy scale and contamination that could bias measurement results. Inspectors must be trained on part handling that can affect hardness readings and bore geometry.

Hardness
Take hardness measurements using a portable Rockwell hardness tester set for the appropriate scale and indenter for HRC readings. Prepare the surface by gentle scale removal without removing base material; abrasive cleaning must be light and should not alter near-surface hardening. Take readings at multiple radial positions around the bore and on flange faces as applicable to identify variability. Reject if any reading falls outside the range. Record location of each reading on the inspection report and include tester identification and last calibration date as part of the record.

Bore diameter
Measure bore diameter using a calibrated bore gauge or inside micrometer appropriate for the feature size. Ensure the measuring instrument is temperature stabilized to ambient workspace conditions to minimize thermal bias. For features requiring finish machining, measure after the final machining operation when applicable; for forged-only acceptance use nominal forged bore dimension with the tolerance shown. Record the instrument used and the measured values; report the deviation from nominal and indicate whether in tolerance per the table.

Mass
Weigh the forging using a floor scale with sufficient capacity and resolution. Tare procedures must be documented; weights must be recorded to show compliance with the maximum forging weight listed. If weight exceeds the maximum forging weight, handle as nonconforming per the nonconformance section. Record scale identification and last calibration date.

Sampling and frequency
For first article inspection, perform full characteristic inspection including hardness mapping, bore diameter measurement, and mass verification. For routine production, perform dimensional sampling per the plant control plan and include hardness checks at a defined frequency adequate to detect process drift. When a process change is introduced, perform verification on the first affected lot.

Data and records
Maintain inspection records in the document control system. Each inspection record shall include part id, lot or heat reference, inspector name or id, instrument id and calibration status, measurement locations, raw readings, pass/fail statement for each characteristic, and disposition. Hardness maps and bore measurement sheets shall be attached to lot records. Retain records in accordance with the plant record retention policy and make them available to quality audits.

Examples and rationale
Example A: A batch of gear blanks arrives for first article inspection. The inspector performs hardness mapping and records values within the required hardness range. Bore checks show measurements within the tolerance band. The batch is accepted and released for machining. Example B: A forging measures slightly outside the allowable bore diameter tolerance after boring. The forging is segregated and tagged; further investigation shows a tooling issue during boring. The lot is placed on hold and nonconformance procedures are invoked.

The rationale for the specified hardness range is to ensure sufficient core strength while allowing for subsequent heat treatment and carburizing processes typical for 8620 steel forgings. The bore diameter tolerance ensures fit-up with mating components and minimizes rework. The maximum forging weight restricts handling and process equipment limits to maintain safe and predictable forging and heat treatment operations.

Nonconformance handling
Segregation and hold
Any item found outside the specified requirements shall be immediately segregated and placed on hold. The inspector shall attach a hold tag and notify the quality engineer and production supervisor. The part shall not proceed to downstream processes until disposition is approved.

Disposition options
Disposition options include rework, repair, or scrap. Rework or repair actions shall be evaluated for technical feasibility and must restore the part to the specified requirements without adversely affecting material properties. All rework shall be documented, and reworked parts shall undergo full inspection of the affected characteristics. Scrap material shall be documented and returned to the scrap system with appropriate traceability.

Root cause and corrective action
For any nonconformance, a root cause analysis shall be performed and a corrective action plan instituted to prevent recurrence. Actions may include tool maintenance, process parameter adjustments, or additional operator training. The quality engineer shall document findings and corrective actions and close the corrective action only after verification of effectiveness.

Disposition records
All nonconformance reports shall include part id, lot or heat reference, characteristic out of tolerance, measured values, disposition decision, rework steps performed if any, and final acceptance verification. These records shall be linked to the original inspection records and retained with the lot file for audit and traceability.

Scope
This quality specification defines metallurgical and dimensional acceptance criteria, inspection methods, and nonconformance handling for bearing ring CFW-4068-79 (CFW-4068-79) forged and processed at Plant P3. It applies to all production lots, in-process operations, and final inspection prior to release for heat treatment and shipment. The intent is to ensure consistent ring hardness, bore geometry, and forging mass requirements are met for downstream finishing and assembly.

Requirements table
- Material: bearing ring CFW-4068-79 (CFW-4068-79) supplied and processed to shop drawings.
- Hardness: The hardness range for bearing ring CFW-4068-79 (CFW-4068-79) is 38-43 HRC.
- Bore diameter tolerance: The bore diameter tolerance for bearing ring CFW-4068-79 (CFW-4068-79) is ±0.07 mm.
- Maximum forging weight: The maximum forging weight for bearing ring CFW-4068-79 (CFW-4068-79) is 114.6 kg.
- Surface condition: rings shall be free of scale, laps, and material separations that would affect machining or part performance.
- Traceability: each ring shall retain the lot identification and furnace ticket linkage through finishing operations.

Notes on requirements and rationale
- Hardness: The stated hardness range is set to ensure the forgings respond predictably to subsequent heat treatment and grinding operations. The range balances wear resistance and toughness for typical bearing ring applications where the steel grade is 52100. Test location and method are chosen to represent bulk material condition rather than localized surface effects.
- Bore tolerance: Bore geometry affects fit-up and final machining stock. The specified tolerance controls the amount of material to be removed during bore finishing and ensures interchangeability at assembly. The tolerance is tight to reduce variable grinding time and to protect heat treat allowances.
- Forging weight: The maximum forging weight is provided to govern die design, press capacity checks, material handling, and process planning. Exceeding the listed maximum requires written approval from Plant P3 engineering before proceeding.

Inspection method
Sampling and location
- Visual inspection: perform visual assessment of the entire ring surface to identify forging defects before any heat treatment or machining. Record observations in the inspection record.
- Hardness measurement: perform hardness testing on the as-forged state at representative circumferential locations and axial positions selected to avoid skives and machining marks. Use a calibrated hardness tester and apply the same test method consistently so values reflect the bulk material condition. Record each reading.
- Bore measurement: measure the bore diameter with a bore gauge or appropriate calibrated metrology instrument. Measurements shall be taken at multiple circumferential positions and at two axial stations to detect out-of-roundness and taper. Record all readings and calculate conformity to the bore diameter tolerance.
- Mass verification: verify forging mass by weighing the ring on a calibrated scale. The measured mass shall not exceed the maximum forging weight specified.

Calibration and equipment
- Use calibrated instruments maintained under the Plant P3 calibration program. Calibration status and certificate reference shall be recorded with the inspection results.
- Hardness tester and bore gauge serial identifiers shall be entered into the inspection record for traceability.

Examples and interpretation
- Example acceptance: if hardness readings at representative locations fall within the stated hardness range, and measured bore diameters at all measured points fall within the specified bore diameter tolerance, and the measured mass does not exceed the maximum forging weight, the ring is acceptable for release to next process.
- Example rejection: if any hardness reading is outside the stated hardness range, or any bore measurement exceeds the permitted tolerance band, or the forging mass exceeds the listed maximum, the ring is nonconforming and subject to the nonconformance handling procedure described below.

Records to keep
- Inspection record for each ring or lot including visual findings, hardness readings with location identifiers, bore measurements with station identifiers, mass measurement, instrument identifiers, and inspector initials.
- Calibration records for hardness tester, bore gauge, and scale referenced to each inspection event.
- Lot traceability documentation linking ring identification to raw material certificate and heat number.
- Disposition documents for any nonconforming items including corrective action and final disposition.

Nonconformance handling
Identification and segregation
- Any item failing to meet the requirements in this specification shall be immediately identified, segregated, and controlled to prevent unintended use. The item shall be marked as nonconforming and logged in the Plant P3 nonconformance register.

Evaluation and disposition
- Engineering evaluation: Plant P3 engineering shall review nonconforming items to determine whether rework, repair, concession, or scrapping is required. Evaluation shall document the nature of the nonconformance, root cause where identifiable, and recommended disposition.
- Concession: a formal concession request may be generated where the deviation does not impact fit, form, or function for the intended application. A concession must be approved in writing by Plant P3 engineering prior to release.
- Rework: where feasible, rework instructions will be issued specifying allowable actions to bring the part into conformance. Reworked items must undergo full inspection per this specification before release.

Corrective action and records
- For systemic or repeated nonconformances, a corrective action record shall be opened to identify root cause, containment actions, and preventive measures. Records shall include inspection data, evaluation conclusions, concession approvals, rework instructions, and final disposition.
- All nonconformance records and dispositions shall be retained as part of the lot file for traceability and audit.

Change control
- Any proposed change to the requirements specified in this document must be submitted through Plant P3 document control and approved before implementation. The revision history must be maintained in the lot file.

End of specification.

Scope
- This quality specification applies to the finished forged valve body CFW-4376-34 manufactured in Plant P3 from material F316. It defines acceptance criteria, inspection methods, handling of nonconforming product, and the records required to demonstrate compliance to the requirements listed below.
- The document covers dimensional and metallurgical acceptance for the valve body CFW-4376-34 and applies at final inspection after all machining and heat treatment operations are complete.

Requirements table
- The table below lists the critical characteristics for valve body CFW-4376-34 (CFW-4376-34). These characteristics are controlled and recorded for every production lot.

| Characteristic | Requirement | Acceptance |
|---|---:|---|
| Hardness range (HRC) | 28-32 HRC | Must fall within 28-32 HRC on representative samples per lot |
| Bore diameter tolerance | ±0.10 mm | Feature must be within nominal bore ±0.10 mm |
| Maximum forging weight | 46.2 kg | Forging weight must not exceed 46.2 kg as stamped or calculated |

- Rationale: Hardness range 28-32 HRC is specified to ensure the balance of strength and machinability for F316 valve bodies. Bore diameter tolerance ±0.10 mm is set to ensure sealing surfaces and mating components meet assembly requirements. Maximum forging weight 46.2 kg constrains forging dies and material flow to maintain mechanical properties and dimensional control.

Inspection method
- Sampling approach: Inspect each finished piece for dimensional conformance and record hardness on a representative sample selected from each production lot. Selection rationale and sampling records are described below.
- Dimensional inspection:
  - Measure the bore diameter with calibrated bore measurement equipment capable of reading to required precision. Confirm the measured value is within nominal bore ±0.10 mm. For clarity, record the nominal bore value on the inspection record and report the measured deviation relative to ±0.10 mm tolerance.
  - Inspect other critical mating features visually and by dimensional check to confirm they will not interfere with the bore requirement. When any feature affects the bore, include a note on the inspection record explaining the relationship.
- Hardness testing:
  - Perform hardness testing on a machined surface representative of the parent material, following surface preparation best practice to remove chips and scale. Record the hardness value and demonstrate compliance with 28-32 HRC.
  - Use a calibrated hardness tester appropriate for the expected hardness range and document calibration status on the test record.
- Weight verification:
  - Verify forging weight by the supplier stamping, weight ticket, or calculated material usage and confirm it does not exceed 46.2 kg. Record the source of weight verification on the inspection form.
- Measurement verification and equipment control:
  - Ensure measurement instruments and hardness testers are within their calibration cycle and traceable to accepted standards. List the instrument identifier and calibration status on each inspection record.
- Example inspection record entries:
  - Bore: nominal value, measured value, pass/fail versus ±0.10 mm.
  - Hardness: measured HRC, hardness test location, pass/fail versus 28-32 HRC.
  - Weight: documented forging weight source and pass/fail versus 46.2 kg.

Nonconformance handling
- Identification and segregation:
  - Any valve body CFW-4376-34 found outside the requirements in the requirements table must be clearly tagged, segregated from acceptable inventory, and logged into the nonconformance system. The log entry must reference the specific characteristic out of tolerance, the measured value, and the inspection record identifier.
- Disposition options:
  - Rework: Where the out-of-tolerance condition is dimensional and can be corrected by documented machining operations without affecting critical characteristics, perform rework only after written approval by the responsible engineering authority. The rework plan must reference the inspected nonconformance and describe controls to prevent recurrence.
  - Reject: If the hardness is outside 28-32 HRC or the forging weight exceeds 46.2 kg and cannot be recovered to meet specification, the part shall be rejected and returned to supplier or scrapped as defined by material disposition rules.
  - Use-as-is by concession: A concession for use-as-is may be issued only by authorized quality personnel when justified by engineering analysis. The concession shall document the nonconforming characteristic, rationale for acceptance, any special marking or restrictions on use, and a reference to the inspection data that shows the deviation.
- Root cause and corrective action:
  - For repeated occurrences of the same nonconformance, perform root cause analysis and implement corrective action to control the process. Document corrective actions, responsible parties, and verification of effectiveness.
- Records to keep:
  - For every production lot, retain the inspection records that show compliance or nonconformance for bore diameter ±0.10 mm, hardness 28-32 HRC, and forging weight 46.2 kg. Include instrument identifiers and calibration evidence.
  - Maintain nonconformance records, disposition decisions, rework plans, and concession approvals in the document control system. Records shall reference the part CFW-4376-34 and the inspection record identifier.
  - Retain supplier weight tickets or stamping evidence when used for forging weight verification.

Background and step rationale
- The hardness requirement 28-32 HRC was selected to meet expected service loads while allowing final machining and sealing operation tolerances. The bore tolerance ±0.10 mm reflects interface requirements with mating seats and stems to ensure leak-tight assembly. Maximum forging weight 46.2 kg controls forging die life and thermal mass for heat treatment uniformity.
- Following the inspection methods above ensures that measurement variability is controlled and documented. Example situations include a bore marginally outside ±0.10 mm that can be corrected by finish machining with documented engineering approval, or a hardness value outside 28-32 HRC indicating heat treatment deviation that requires batch-level investigation.

# QS-CFW-5042-83 - Quality specification - valve body CFW-5042-83 (F316)

Scope
This quality specification applies to the valve body CFW-5042-83 (F316) manufactured and processed at Plant P3. It defines the acceptance criteria, inspection methods, and nonconformance handling for incoming forgings, in-process operations, and final inspection prior to release for assembly or shipment. Background rationale: the valve body is a pressure-retaining component whose mechanical properties and dimensional accuracy are critical to performance. The requirements below are selected to ensure material integrity, interchangeability, and traceable disposition.

Requirements table
The table lists critical acceptance criteria that must be verified and recorded for each lot of parts of CFW-5042-83.

| Characteristic | Requirement | Acceptance |
|---|---:|---|
| Material designation | F316 forging | Conforms to material certification trace |
| Hardness (as-heat-treated) | 33-38 HRC | All sampled parts must fall within the range 33-38 HRC |
| Critical bore diameter | ±0.06 mm | Measured diameter must be within drawing nominal ±0.06 mm |
| Maximum forging weight | 61.8 kg | Any forging exceeding 61.8 kg is rejected for this part number |
| Surface condition | Free of forging laps and scale that affect machinability and sealing surfaces | Visual and tactile acceptance; see inspection method below |

Notes on table entries and rationale:
- Hardness: the specified hardness range 33-38 HRC balances machinability and required strength for service. Hardness testing provides a rapid check that heat treatment cycles have produced the intended metallurgical condition.
- Bore tolerance: tight bore control to ±0.06 mm ensures gasket and mating component fit. This tolerance reflects downstream assembly needs and sealing performance.
- Maximum forging weight: the maximum forging weight 61.8 kg is defined to control furnace charging, forging press capacity, and subsequent machining fixtures. Exceeding weight may indicate an incorrect die or material charge.
- Surface condition: defects that interfere with machining or sealing are unacceptable; cosmetic imperfections that do not affect function may be dispositioned per standard practice but must be recorded.

Inspection method
Sampling and records
- Each incoming lot of CFW-5042-83 forgings must be assigned a unique lot record in the document control system and retained with inspection results and material certificates. For each lot, record the supplier batch, heat number trace from the mill certificate, and number of pieces inspected.
- Hardness testing: perform hardness tests on representative locations on each inspected part after final heat treatment and prior to finish machining. Use a calibrated Rockwell C hardness tester. Record individual readings and the test instrument ID and calibration due status in the lot record. If any reading falls outside 33-38 HRC, quarantine the lot and initiate nonconformance handling.
- Dimensional inspection: measure the critical bore diameter using a calibrated bore gauge or coordinate measuring machine. Measurements shall be taken at a minimum of two axial locations and two circumferential positions to detect out-of-round and taper conditions. Record all measurements. Acceptance is per ±0.06 mm.
- Weight verification: confirm forging weight by using calibrated scales. Record the measured weight for the inspected piece. If measured weight exceeds 61.8 kg, segregate the item and tag as over-weight.
- Surface inspection: perform visual inspection under appropriate lighting and tactile verification for laps, folds, or scale that would affect further processing. Document findings with photos when defects are present.
- Calibration and traceability: maintain calibration certificates for hardness tester, bore gauge, CMM, and scales. Include instrument ID and calibration status in inspection records.

Examples and step rationale
- Example: if a lot of five forgings is received, record the supplier heat number and inspect each piece according to the sampling plan established for this part. Hardness readings of 34 HRC, 35 HRC, and 36 HRC are acceptable because they fall in the range 33-38 HRC. A bore measurement of nominal plus 0.05 mm is within ±0.06 mm and acceptable. A piece weighing 62.0 kg must be segregated because it exceeds 61.8 kg.
- Rationale: providing concrete examples clarifies how to interpret the numeric requirements and supports consistent dispositions across inspection personnel.

Records to keep
- Lot inspection record including supplier information, heat numbers, and disposition status.
- Hardness test records showing locations, individual readings, and tester ID.
- Dimensional inspection reports showing raw measurements, instrument used, and inspector initials.
- Weight verification records with scale ID and measured weight.
- Photographic evidence and defect descriptions for any nonconformances.
- Calibration certificates for all measuring instruments referenced above.
All records must be retained in the document control system as part of the lot history and available for audit.

Nonconformance handling
Disposition procedure
- Any part or lot that fails to meet the hardness requirement of 33-38 HRC, the bore diameter tolerance of ±0.06 mm, or the maximum forging weight of 61.8 kg shall be immediately segregated and labeled as nonconforming.
- Initiate a nonconformance report that documents the specific parameter out of tolerance, associated measurements, and supporting material certificate information. Include recommended disposition: return to supplier, rework if feasible, or scrap. Rework options must be reviewed and approved by engineering and quality; rework must restore the part to meet the listed requirements before release.
- Investigations: for systemic or repeated failures, perform a root cause investigation to determine whether the issue arises from supplier controls, heat treatment process, die wear, or handling. Document corrective actions and verify effectiveness through follow-up inspections.
Examples of disposition actions
- A forging outside the hardness range: quarantine and review heat-treatment records. If hardness can be corrected by an approved heat treatment procedure, detail the procedure and required verification tests before release.
- A forging outside the bore tolerance: determine if machining allowances remain to bring the bore into tolerance. If not, declare the part nonconforming and follow the nonconformance report for supplier return or scrap.
- A forging exceeding the maximum forging weight of 61.8 kg: segregate and hold. Confirm whether the part matches the drawing and part number; if it does not, treat as incorrect part and return to supplier.

Audit and review
- Quality shall periodically review inspection records and nonconformance trends for CFW-5042-83 to confirm ongoing compliance with the requirements listed in this specification. Any changes to acceptance criteria must be approved through the document change process.

This specification is mandatory for production, quality, and shipping personnel responsible for release and disposition of CFW-5349-60 components.

## Requirements table
| Characteristic | Requirement | Acceptance criteria | Record |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Material | Material grade and traceability as per purchase order | Conforming mill certificate and heat number present | Purchase order and mill certificate filed with inspection report |
| Hardness | Rockwell hardness of heat-treated link body | The hardness range for track link CFW-5349-60 (CFW-5349-60) is 33-36 HRC. | Hardness test report attached to lot inspection record |
| Bore diameter | Final machined bore diameter tolerance | The bore diameter tolerance for track link CFW-5349-60 (CFW-5349-60) is ±0.03 mm. | Dimensional inspection checklist and CMM printout |
| Forging weight | Gross forging weight limit per forging | The maximum forging weight for track link CFW-5349-60 (CFW-5349-60) is 58.0 kg. | Forging log and weight ticket retained with lot record |
| Surface condition | No cracks, laps, or other forging defects affecting function | Visual and NDT acceptance; no through-thickness defects | Visual inspection report and NDT report |
| Functional fit | Assembly fit and movement as defined on drawing | Part must assemble without interference and allow intended articulation | Assembly verification record |

Notes:
- All acceptance criteria must be met before parts are released from Final Inspection.
- Records identified above must be retained in the part lot file and be available for audit.

## Inspection method
Overview: Inspections shall be performed at the operations defined by production routing: post-heat-treat, post-machining, and final inspection prior to release. Inspectors shall be trained in the methods described below and shall record results on the lot inspection report.

Hardness testing:
- Method: Use Rockwell C scale test per laboratory procedure. Test locations are the bore hub and link body at the location of expected maximum hardness variation. Indentations shall be placed to avoid interference with mating surfaces.
- Sampling rationale: Choose representative samples across the lot to capture process variability and to confirm case hardness meets the specification above. If hardness readings approach specification limits, increase sampling density to fully characterize the lot and include results in the inspection report.
- Documentation: Record the instrument ID, calibration status, operator initials, and individual reading locations on the hardness test sheet. Attach the hardness test sheet to the lot inspection record.

Bore diameter measurement:
- Method: Measure finished bore diameter using a calibrated bore gauge or CMM. Measurements shall be taken at multiple radial positions and along the bore axis to detect eccentricity or taper; report the worst-case dimension relative to the nominal and tolerance requirement noted above.
- Acceptance: Confirm that the measured deviation from nominal does not exceed the tolerance specified in the requirements table. Measurements that fall outside the stated tolerance require immediate hold and disposition.
- Documentation: Include measurement printouts and gauge identification with the lot record.

Forging weight verification:
- Method: Weigh each forging on a calibrated scale after trimming and cooling. Record the gross forging weight on the forging log. Verify that the item does not exceed the maximum forging weight listed in the requirements table.
- Examples: If a forging weight equals or exceeds the listed maximum forging weight, the piece is to be segregated and processed under nonconformance handling.

Visual and NDT inspection:
- Method: Perform visual inspection for surface defects at specified inspection stations. Where required, perform magnetic particle or dye penetrant inspection per standard procedures to identify near-surface defects.
- Documentation: Retain NDT reports and acceptance stamps in the lot file.

Final functional check:
- Method: Fit a sample from the lot into the assembly fixture or mating part to confirm articulation and fit. Record any adverse fit conditions and include photographic evidence when deviations occur.

Records and traceability:
- Each lot file must include mill certificates, heat numbers, hardness test report, bore measurement data, forging weight ticket, visual/NDT reports, inspector identifiers, and final release signature. These records support traceability from raw material to finished part.

## Nonconformance handling
Identification and segregation:
- Any part or lot that fails to meet the requirements listed in the Requirements table shall be immediately identified and segregated from conforming stock. Use a hold tag and record the nonconformance in the quality system.

Notification and containment:
- Notify production supervision and quality engineering when a nonconformance is detected. Containment actions shall include quarantine of suspect lots, review of process parameters, and temporary suspension of shipments for affected lots.

Evaluation and disposition:
- Quality engineering shall evaluate the root cause and impact on fit, form, and function. Disposition options include rework, repair, downgrade for allowable noncritical applications, or scrap. Rework plans must be documented and approved by quality engineering prior to execution.

Examples:
- Hardness out of range: If measured hardness is outside the hardness range for track link CFW-5349-60 (CFW-5349-60) is 33-36 HRC., the lot is placed on hold. A heat-treatment review and retest protocol shall be executed before any release.
- Bore out of tolerance: If bore measurements exceed the bore diameter tolerance for track link CFW-5349-60 (CFW-5349-60) is ±0.03 mm., the lot shall be reviewed for machining rework or separation for scrap.
- Overweight forging: Forgings found to exceed the maximum forging weight for track link CFW-5349-60 (CFW-5349-60) is 58.0 kg. shall be quarantined pending metallurgical review to determine if material condition is acceptable or if material should be scrapped.

Disposition records:
- All nonconformance evaluations, root cause analyses, corrective actions, and final dispositions must be recorded in the quality system and attached to the lot file. These records are evidence of correction and are subject to internal and customer audits.

Revision control:
- This is Rev C of QS-CFW-5349-60 and supersedes Rev B. All previously issued copies shall be archived with their revision history and superseded controlled copies shall be marked as obsolete.

# QS-CFW-5798-88 — Quality specification - crankshaft blank CFW-5798-88 (4340)
Revision: Rev E  
Plant: P2  
Parts: CFW-5798-88  
This revision supersedes Rev D.

Scope
- This quality specification applies to crankshaft blank CFW-5798-88 (4340) manufactured at Plant P2 and intended for subsequent machining and heat treatment operations at external or internal facilities. It defines the acceptance criteria, inspection methods, and nonconformance handling for receiving, in-process, and final inspection of the forged blank prior to release for downstream processing.

Background and rationale
- The material and geometry of CFW-5798-88 require control of core hardness, bore tolerance, and blank mass to ensure compatibility with downstream machining centers and final part requirements. The specified hardness range balances machinability and microstructural condition for successful heat treatment and finish grinding. The specified bore diameter tolerance ensures fitment to fixture bores used in machining operations without additional rework. The maximum forging weight is controlled to prevent overloading of handling equipment and to maintain consistency in forming parameters that affect internal soundness.

Requirements table

| Characteristic | Requirement | Acceptance |
|---|---:|---|
| Material designation | 4340 | Conforming mill certificate required |
| Hardness (as-forged core) | 25-29 HRC | Accept if within range; reject if outside range |
| Bore diameter tolerance | ±0.04 mm | Accept if measured within tolerance relative to drawing datum |
| Maximum forging weight | 119.4 kg | Do not accept blanks exceeding this mass |
| Surface condition | No visible laps, folds, or unbonded surface; light forging scale acceptable | Reject if surface discontinuities compromise geometry or machining allowance |
| Internal soundness | No indication of internal voids by method specified below | Reject if evidence of internal discontinuity is detected |

Inspection method
- Receiving inspection: Verify material certificate matches 4340 and traceability to heat lot. Physically verify identification marking against part serial. Measure mass using calibrated scales; record mass and compare to maximum forging weight of 119.4 kg. For any blank with mass exceeding 119.4 kg, segregate and initiate nonconformance procedure.
- Hardness measurement: Perform hardness testing on the as-forged core using a calibrated hardness tester appropriate for HRC scale. Take a representative reading in the mid-section of the crankshaft blank avoiding fillet radii and surface-affected zones. Report the measured value and verify it falls within 25-29 HRC. If a reading is outside 25-29 HRC, perform two additional measurements on nominally equivalent locations and record all readings. If any reading remains outside 25-29 HRC, follow nonconformance handling.
- Bore diameter measurement: Measure the bore diameter at the specified inspection plane using a calibrated bore gauge or plug gage capable of resolving to the required tolerance. Verify the measured diameter is within ±0.04 mm of the nominal drawing dimension at the inspection plane. Record the measurement method, instrument identification, and operator initials. If measurement uncertainty is suspected, perform a repeat measurement with an alternate calibrated instrument and document both results.
- Internal soundness inspection: Inspect for internal discontinuities using the non-destructive method specified in the drawing package. Record the inspection technique used and the operator identification. Any indication consistent with internal voids or laps is cause for rejection; document findings and proceed with nonconformance handling.
- Sampling and frequency: Determine inspection frequency based on the lot size and risk assessment performed by quality engineering. Document the chosen sampling plan and the rationale. Maintain records of the sampling plan in the part inspection folder.
- Calibration and instrument control: Ensure all measurement equipment used for mass, hardness, and bore measurement is within valid calibration. Record calibration certificate reference numbers in the inspection records.

Nonconformance handling
- Identification and segregation: Any blank failing to meet the requirements listed in the requirements table must be immediately identified, tagged, and segregated from conforming material to prevent inadvertent use. Use a nonconformance tag referencing this document id.
- Disposition options: Possible dispositions include rework, return to vendor, conditional acceptance for non-critical use, or scrap. Determine disposition based on root cause analysis, potential impact to fit and function, and consultation with the responsible engineering authority. For mass nonconformances exceeding the maximum forging weight of 119.4 kg, consider tooling and process review before dispositioning similar future pieces.
- Root cause and corrective action: For any nonconformance, perform a documented root cause analysis and implement corrective actions to prevent recurrence. Record corrective action assignments, responsible parties, and verification activities in the nonconformance record.
- Examples:
  - Example A: If a blank measures 24 HRC on initial hardness reading, perform two additional hardness measurements in equivalent locations. If the additional readings remain below the acceptable range of 25-29 HRC, record the measurements and initiate nonconformance handling to determine cause and disposition.
  - Example B: If a bore measurement shows a deviation beyond ±0.04 mm at the inspection plane, confirm instrument calibration and repeat measurement. If confirmed, segregate and document as nonconforming; investigate press and die condition for potential tooling wear.
- Records to keep: Maintain the following records in the part inspection folder: material mill certificate, mass measurement record (including instrument id), hardness test records (including instrument id and all readings), bore measurement records (including instrument id and drawing datum reference), internal soundness inspection report, calibration certificates for instruments used, nonconformance records, root cause analysis, and final disposition documentation. All records must reference QS-CFW-5798-88 and the applicable lot or serial identifiers for traceability.
- Review and release: Quality engineering shall review all inspection records before release of the blank for downstream processing. Release is permitted only when all specified requirements are met or a documented approved deviation exists.

End of document.
