# QS-CFW-5998-73 — Quality specification - track link CFW-5998-73 (15B37)  
Revision: Rev B (This revision supersedes Rev A)  
Plant: P2  
Parts: CFW-5998-73

Scope
This quality specification defines the acceptance criteria, inspection methods, and nonconformance handling for the track link CFW-5998-73 (CFW-5998-73). It applies to forged and machined finished parts produced and accepted at Plant P2 and to any external vendor supply of identical items where this document is referenced. The purpose is to ensure mechanical integrity and interchangeability for assembly. Background commentary explains why the listed requirements are controlled and how inspection decisions are to be recorded for traceability.

Requirements table
The following key characteristics are controlled as specified. These are the only numeric acceptance criteria permitted by this document.

- Characteristic: Hardness  
  Requirement: The hardness range for track link CFW-5998-73 (CFW-5998-73) is 31-35 HRC.  
  Rationale: Hardness is controlled to ensure wear resistance while maintaining required toughness for service. The specified range is the result of design validation and field feedback indicating acceptable service life without increased susceptibility to brittle failure.

- Characteristic: Bore diameter tolerance  
  Requirement: The bore diameter tolerance for track link CFW-5998-73 (CFW-5998-73) is ±0.08 mm.  
  Rationale: Bore concentricity and fit are critical for pin assembly and articulation. The stated tolerance preserves assembly clearance and prevents accelerated wear or binding in service.

- Characteristic: Maximum forging weight  
  Requirement: The maximum forging weight for track link CFW-5998-73 (CFW-5998-73) is 4.8 kg.  
  Rationale: Limiting forging weight controls material usage, thermal gradients during cooling, and handling limits on forging equipment. Maintaining the maximum weight ensures consistent microstructure and reduces the risk of internal defects.

Inspection method
Overview: Inspections shall be performed using calibrated equipment and documented procedures. Acceptance decisions shall reference the requirements table above. Inspectors shall be trained on part-specific tooling and on methods described below.

Hardness measurement: Use an appropriate hardness test method compatible with HRC scale and the part geometry. Measurements shall be taken in locations representative of the bearing surfaces and heat-treated region. The inspector shall avoid surface anomalies and ensure adequate surface preparation prior to testing. For irregular geometry, select a testing location that reflects worst-case service loading. Record individual test locations and their readings in the inspection record. Compare each recorded reading to the hardness requirement: the hardness range for track link CFW-5998-73 (CFW-5998-73) is 31-35 HRC.

Bore diameter inspection: Bore diameter shall be measured with gauging or coordinate inspection capable of resolving the tolerance band specified. Use plug gauges, air gauges, or CMM probing as appropriate to the production environment and part accessibility. Measure multiple positions around the bore to detect ovality and taper. Record nominal diameter, measured deviations, and the applied measurement method in the inspection record. Compare results against the bore diameter tolerance for track link CFW-5998-73 (CFW-5998-73): ±0.08 mm.

Weight verification: Forging weight shall be verified prior to machining using calibrated scales or process weighing equipment appropriate for the forging environment. The measured forging weight must not exceed the maximum forging weight for track link CFW-5998-73 (CFW-5998-73): 4.8 kg. Record the forging weight and the equipment identification in the lot record. If weight is near the limit, document actions taken and any process adjustments.

Traceability and records: For each inspected lot, the inspector shall produce an inspection record that contains at minimum: part identifier, lot or heat identifier, machine or cell identifier, specific measurement results for the characteristics listed in the requirements table, identification of measurement equipment used, and the signature or electronic approval of the inspector. These records shall be retained per Plant P2 record retention policy and shall be made available for engineering review or customer audit.

Sampling and special cases: If statistical sampling is used, the sampling plan must be documented separately and approved by Quality prior to use. When irregular parts, repair operations, or alternate suppliers are involved, Quality shall be notified and a disposition plan created before release.

Nonconformance handling
Identification: Any part that fails to meet one or more of the requirements in the requirements table is nonconforming. Mark nonconforming parts to prevent inadvertent use and segregate them from conforming stock.

Evaluation and disposition: Nonconforming parts shall be evaluated by Quality together with Engineering to determine the root cause and appropriate disposition. Disposition options include rework, repair, concession, or scrap. Decisions shall be documented and include rationale. When a concession is considered, justification shall include assessment of service impact and risk, and the customer shall be notified if contractual requirements demand.

Examples:
- Example disposition scenario: A bore measured outside the bore diameter tolerance for track link CFW-5998-73 (CFW-5998-73) is subject to evaluation. If rework to bring the bore within ±0.08 mm is feasible without compromising heat treatment or geometry, rework instructions and controls shall be documented and reinspection performed. If rework is not feasible, the part is to be scrapped or returned to vendor per disposition.
- Example hardness scenario: A part with localized hardness below the range of 31-35 HRC requires root cause analysis focusing on heat-treatment parameters and quench uniformity. If localized softness is attributable to process deviation, affected lot is quarantined pending containment and corrective actions.

Containment and corrective action: When a systemic nonconformance is identified, Quality shall initiate containment to prevent additional nonconforming production. Root cause analysis shall be performed, corrective action implemented, and effectiveness verified. Records of containment and corrective actions, including affected lots and dates, shall be retained.

Records to keep
Maintain the following records for each lot or heat as part of the part history file:
- Inspection record containing measured hardness values and test locations, with equipment identifiers and operator approval. Ensure that the hardness range for track link CFW-5998-73 (CFW-5998-73) is clearly referenced.
- Bore measurement record showing measured values and method, with documentation that results comply with the bore diameter tolerance for track link CFW-5998-73 (CFW-5998-73): ±0.08 mm.
- Forging weight record showing pre-machining weight and verification that the forging weight does not exceed the maximum forging weight for track link CFW-5998-73 (CFW-5998-73): 4.8 kg.
- Nonconformance reports and dispositions, including root cause analysis and corrective action verification when applicable.

Change control
This document is controlled under document number QS-CFW-5998-73. Revisions shall be authorized by Engineering and Quality. This revision is Rev B and supersedes Rev A; any superseded copies shall be identified as obsolete and removed from active use.

Revision: Rev E  
This revision supersedes Rev D.  
Plant: P1  
Parts: CFW-6160-72

Scope
This quality specification applies to the manufacturing, inspection, and disposition of crankshaft blank CFW-6160-72 (4340) produced at Plant P1. It defines acceptance criteria, inspection methods, records to retain, and nonconformance handling for forgings delivered as crankshaft blanks for downstream machining and heat treatment. It is intended for use by production, quality, and inspection personnel responsible for in-process and final inspection prior to release to stock.

Requirements table
| Characteristic | Requirement | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Material | 4340 per purchase order | Verify material traceability to mill certificate. |
| Hardness | The hardness range for crankshaft blank CFW-6160-72 (CFW-6160-72) is 26-31 HRC. | Hardness measured on machined witness coupons or lightly machined surface as specified in inspection method. |
| Bore diameter tolerance | The bore diameter tolerance for crankshaft blank CFW-6160-72 (CFW-6160-72) is ±0.07 mm. | Tolerance applies to finish bore after any required sizing operation described in manufacturing routing. |
| Forging weight | The maximum forging weight for crankshaft blank CFW-6160-72 (CFW-6160-72) is 22.9 kg. | Weight to be recorded on heat traveler and final inspection report. |
| Surface condition | Forging surfaces shall be free of discontinuities that affect fit or safety | Visible scale and minor laps may be trimmed; subsurface indications of concern to be evaluated per nonconformance handling. |
| Traceability | Each piece must be linked to heat and lot documentation | Include mill certificate and internal heat traveler with each shipment. |

Inspection method
Overview
Inspection includes material verification, dimensional checks, hardness testing, weight confirmation, and surface evaluation. Inspectors shall follow the sequential steps below and document results on the final inspection record.

Material verification
Confirm mill certificate matches the part serials and heat lot on the heat traveler. Verify chemistry and hardness acceptance on the certificate prior to proceeding with dimensional checks.

Dimensional inspection
Perform dimensional checks on the finish bore and critical mating features. For the finish bore, confirm compliance with bore diameter tolerance. Use calibrated bore gauges or equivalent measuring equipment that provide traceability to national standards. When a bore does not meet the tolerance, do not release the part; proceed to nonconformance handling.

Hardness testing
Hardness sampling shall be taken from designated witness coupons or from a machined area that does not compromise the part. Hardness testing shall be performed with a calibrated indenter appropriate for the hardness scale. Record hardness readings and ensure they fall within the specified hardness range.

Weight confirmation
Weigh each crankshaft blank and record the measured weight on the heat traveler and final inspection record. Ensure the measured weight does not exceed the maximum forging weight.

Surface inspection
Visually inspect all machined and unmachined surfaces for cracks, laps, folds, or other discontinuities. Subsurface or suspected internal indications identified by visual inspection shall be evaluated by appropriate NDE when required by the routing or when the indication cannot be isolated by finishing operations.

Examples and rationale
Example: If a batch of blanks returns a hardness reading outside the specified range, the root cause might be an issue with furnace charge mixing or quench media. Hardness out of range affects downstream machining allowances, fatigue performance, and heat treatment response; therefore, it is critical to capture hardness on both mill certificates and in-process tests to prevent assembly or service failures.
Rationale: The hardness range was selected to ensure sufficient as-forged strength and ductility to withstand downstream handling and the thermal cycles of heat treatment. The bore tolerance reflects the need for accurate alignment in mating assemblies and allows for controlled finishing operations without excessive material removal. The maximum forging weight is a handling and tooling limit for plant equipment and is enforced to prevent equipment overload and ensure safe handling.

Records to keep
Maintain the following records in the document control system and attach them to the heat traveler:
- Material mill certificate and chemistry declaration.
- Final inspection report including hardness readings, bore measurements, and weight entry.
- Heat traveler documenting furnace, process steps, and any deviations.
- Nonconformance report and disposition documentation where applicable.
Records shall be retained in accordance with the company retention policy and made available for customer audits and internal review.

Nonconformance handling
Identification
Any deviation from the requirements table, including material, hardness, bore tolerance, weight limits, or surface integrity, shall be documented immediately as a nonconformance condition.

Containment
Affected parts shall be segregated and clearly labeled pending disposition. Do not return suspect parts to stock or ship to customer without approved disposition.

Disposition and corrective action
Disposition options include rework, reheat, rejection, or use-as-is with concession when permitted by authorized engineering or quality personnel. For example, a bore outside the specified tolerance may be corrected by an approved machining operation if sufficient material remains and downstream fit is verified; otherwise, the blank shall be rejected. Corrective action shall identify root cause and preventive measures to eliminate recurrence.

Escalation and approval
Disposition decisions must be recorded on the nonconformance report and authorized by designated quality or engineering approvers before any action. Records of approval and implemented corrective actions shall be appended to the affected heat traveler.

Audit and review
Periodic review of inspection records, nonconformance trends, and corrective actions shall be conducted to ensure continuous improvement and compliance with this specification. Audit findings that indicate systemic issues shall prompt review of processes, tooling, and personnel training.

Appendix
Definitions, calibration references, and specific tooling instructions are maintained in internal work instructions and process documents. See the document control system index for associated work instructions and calibration procedures.

# QS-CFW-6874-71 - Quality specification - gear blank CFW-6874-71 (8620)
Revision: Rev C (This revision supersedes Rev B)  
Plant: P1  
Parts: CFW-6874-71

Scope
This quality specification defines the acceptance criteria and inspection practices for the gear blank CFW-6874-71 (CFW-6874-71) manufactured at Plant P1. It covers material acknowledgement, hardness and dimensional acceptance at raw forging stage, maximum forging weight control during production, routine inspection methods, example decision rules for disposition, and required records. The intent is to ensure consistent downstream machining and heat-treatment outcomes for parts processed from this forging stock.

Background and rationale
CFW-6874-71 is produced from forging stock intended for subsequent machining and heat treatment to final gear geometry. Controlling core hardness at the blank stage, bore size accuracy, and limiting forging weight variability are essential to meet downstream process capability and to avoid scrap or rework. Hardness affects machinability and quench response; bore tolerance controls fit-up for machining fixtures and subsequent alignment operations; maximum forging weight ensures safe handling and compatibility with plant handling equipment.

Requirements table
The following table lists the critical acceptance criteria for the gear blank CFW-6874-71 (CFW-6874-71). All values are mandatory.

| Characteristic | Requirement | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| Hardness (as-forged) | 41-44 HRC | Measured on core cross-section after normalization; average of three readings per sample. |
| Bore diameter tolerance | ±0.07 mm | Applies to finished bore dimension at forging stage prior to any machining. |
| Maximum forging weight | 130.4 kg | Includes any integral draft or flash; part must not exceed this weight for handling compatibility. |

Inspection method
General approach
Inspection activities shall be planned to verify the Requirements table. Sampling frequency and lot definition are managed by the plant quality plan; inspectors shall follow the plant quality plan for selection of samples. For each sampled blank, perform the sequence below.

Hardness measurement
- Prepare a cross-section through the core at the location representative of the gear tooth bore area. Surface finish must be sufficient for accurate indentation.
- Use a calibrated Rockwell hardness tester set to the appropriate scale for the material. Take three indentations spaced apart within the core region and record individual values.
- Calculate the average of the three readings. Acceptance requires the average to fall within 41-44 HRC. If the average is outside the specified range, see Nonconformance handling.

Bore diameter verification
- Measure the bore diameter using a calibrated bore gauge or coordinate measurement equipment capable of resolving the specified tolerance.
- Record the nominal measured diameter and indicate deviation relative to the intended nominal dimension. The permissible deviation is ±0.07 mm.
- If the measured value falls outside ±0.07 mm, tag the part and initiate disposition per Nonconformance handling.

Forging weight control
- Weigh the as-forged blank on calibrated scales. Record the gross forging weight.
- Verify that the recorded weight is not greater than 130.4 kg. If the weight exceeds 130.4 kg, do not move the part to downstream stations until disposition is decided as per Nonconformance handling.

Examples and decision rationale
- Example: If the hardness readings are 42 HRC, 43 HRC, and 42 HRC, the average is within 41-44 HRC; accept the blank and forward to machining.
- Example: If the bore measurement is nominal plus 0.08 mm relative to target, this exceeds ±0.07 mm; the blank must be segregated for review.
- Example: If the forging weight reads 130.4 kg exactly, the blank meets maximum weight and may proceed; if the reading is above 130.4 kg, hold for review.

Nonconformance handling
Identification and segregation
- Any blank failing to meet any criterion in the Requirements table shall be immediately tagged with a nonconformance identifier and physically segregated from conforming material. Entry into downstream processes is prohibited until disposition is recorded.

Containment and evaluation
- The first action is containment: stop movement of suspect parts and notify quality supervision. Record the nonconformance with the affected characteristic and measurement evidence (hardness readings, bore measurements, weight).
- Perform an evaluation to determine root cause and assess rework feasibility. For hardness out of range, evaluate whether heat-treatment or normalization parameters were applied correctly at the forge. For bore out-of-tolerance, evaluate whether machining allowances or mandrel settings during forging were correct. For weight excess, review die trimming and flash operations.

Disposition options
- Accept with repair: If a documented repair path exists that will restore compliance without compromising downstream performance, document the repair steps and re-inspect after repair.
- Rework: If rework can reliably achieve the specification and is documented in the plant rework procedure, perform rework under controlled conditions and re-inspect.
- Scrap: If the part cannot be returned to specification without risk to final part integrity, document scrapping and material disposition.
- Escalate: If root cause is unknown or indicates systemic process issues, escalate to process engineering for corrective action.

Records to keep
For each lot and for each nonconformance event maintain:
- Hardness test records including individual readings and averaged result for each sampled blank.
- Bore measurement records with instrument identification and operator initials.
- Forging weight records with scale identification.
- Nonconformance record including identifier, characteristic failed, evidence, containment actions, disposition decision, and signature of responsible quality authority.
- Corrective action records when systemic issues are identified, including investigation findings and implemented corrective actions.

Retention and traceability
Maintain records in the plant document control system in accordance with plant procedures to ensure traceability of inspection evidence to the batch and heat lot of the forging material.

Revision control
This document is Rev C and supersedes Rev B. Any changes to the acceptance criteria or inspection methods require formal revision and approval under plant document control.

End of specification.

# QS-CFW-7189-64 Quality specification - bearing ring CFW-7189-64 (52100)
Revision: Rev C — This revision supersedes Rev B  
Plant: P1  
Parts: CFW-7189-64

## Scope
This quality specification defines the acceptance criteria, inspection methods, and nonconformance handling for bearing ring CFW-7189-64 (CFW-7189-64) manufactured from material grade 52100 at Plant P1. The document applies to all forged and finish-processed rings delivered as production parts and to internal rework where dimensional or metallurgical restorative operations are required. Background rationale is provided to explain each requirement and to aid inspection personnel in interpreting results.

## Requirements table
The following table lists the mandatory quality attributes for CFW-7189-64. These attributes are the basis for acceptance at receiving inspection, in-process inspection, and final inspection before shipment.

- Part: CFW-7189-64
- Material: 52100
- Hardness range: 22-26 HRC.
- Bore diameter tolerance: ±0.06 mm.
- Maximum forging weight: 22.9 kg.

Rationale and notes:
- Hardness range 22-26 HRC. is specified to ensure the bearing ring achieves the required balance between wear resistance and toughness for the intended application without additional post-heat-treatment requirements beyond normal process controls. The selected range reflects legacy design constraints and in-service performance history.
- Bore diameter tolerance ±0.06 mm. is specified to ensure proper interference/fit relationships with mating components when finish machining or grinding to final dimensions. The tolerance is applied to the nominal bore dimension called out on the engineering drawing for CFW-7189-64.
- Maximum forging weight 22.9 kg. is a manufacturing constraint that governs furnace charge planning, die loading limits, and handling equipment capacity. All forgings for this part number must not exceed this mass as produced from the forging operation.

## Inspection method
Overview:
Inspection personnel shall perform measurements and tests using calibrated equipment and documented procedures. All measurement equipment used to verify the requirements in this document must be calibrated and traceable to the plant calibration system. The following methods describe how to verify each requirement in the table.

Hardness verification:
- Measure hardness on representative surfaces of the bearing ring using the plant-approved hardness tester and probe suitable for subscale parts. Select at least two locations circumferentially spaced and representative of material condition. Record measurements and compare to the hardness requirement 22-26 HRC.. If the average of readings meets the range and no single reading is outside the band by a margin greater than measurement uncertainty, accept the part; otherwise proceed to nonconformance handling.
- Rationale: Multiple readings mitigate localized surface effects. Recording locations allows trend analysis of heat treatment uniformity.

Bore diameter verification:
- Measure the bore using an inside micrometer, bore gauge, or other calibrated measurement device capable of resolving the specified tolerance. Verify that the measured bore dimension falls within the drawing nominal plus or minus the bore diameter tolerance ±0.06 mm.. Document tool serial numbers and calibration identifiers in the inspection record.
- Example: For a nominal bore dimension shown on the drawing, calculate the acceptable limits by applying ±0.06 mm. to that nominal. Report actual measured value and pass/fail status on the inspection form.

Forging weight verification:
- Verify forging weight at completion of the hot forging operation by weighing the cooled blank on a calibrated scale. Confirm that the as-forged weight does not exceed Maximum forging weight 22.9 kg.. Record the measured weight on the forging log and link to the part lot number.
- Rationale: Weight checks prevent overcharge conditions and help ensure die fill and dimensional stability. The recorded weight assists in root-cause analysis if downstream nonconformances occur.

Measurement records to keep:
- Hardness measurement sheet with part identifier, measurement locations, individual readings, tester identifier, and pass/fail determination.
- Bore measurement sheet listing tool used, calibration ID, measured value, inspector initials, and pass/fail status.
- Forging log entry with scale calibration ID, measured weight, operator initials, and any deviation notes.
- All records shall be retained in the plant quality records system and indexed by part number CFW-7189-64 and lot identifier.

## Nonconformance handling
Detection and initial response:
- Any measurement that fails to meet the specified requirements in the Requirements table is a nonconformance. The inspector shall segregate the affected parts and flag them with the nonconformance identifier used locally. The inspector shall notify the on-shift quality lead and document the findings in the nonconformance log.

Containment and evaluation:
- Contain all affected items to prevent inadvertent use. Perform a documented evaluation to determine the extent of condition, including review of upstream process parameters, heat-treatment records, tooling condition, and prior inspection data. Use the retained records described above to support the evaluation.

Disposition options:
- Rework may be considered if the nonconformance is correctable without jeopardizing part integrity and if the rework method is documented, approved by engineering, and results in full compliance with this specification. Any rework plan shall include verification steps that demonstrate attainment of the requirements: hardness range 22-26 HRC., bore diameter ±0.06 mm., and that final forged mass remains within Maximum forging weight 22.9 kg. where applicable.
- Scrap or return to supplier may be required when rework is not feasible or when metallurgical defects compromise service life. The quality lead shall record the disposition rationale in the nonconformance report.

Records and root cause:
- For each nonconformance event, prepare a report that includes measurement data, inspection records, containment actions, evaluation results, proposed disposition, and verification evidence after disposition. Retain these reports in the quality records system for trending and corrective action planning.

Examples:
- Example inspection entries and typical rework verification steps shall be maintained in the plant procedural library and referenced by inspection personnel during training. These examples must always be reconciled with the requirements stated in this specification before application.

Revision control:
- This document is Rev C and supersedes Rev B. Any future changes shall be processed through the plant document control workflow and linked to the retained inspection and nonconformance records for traceability.

# QS-CFW-7434-20 - Quality specification - connecting rod CFW-7434-20 (1045)

Revision: Rev C  
Plant: P2  
Parts: CFW-7434-20  
Note: This revision supersedes Rev B.

Scope
This quality specification defines the acceptance criteria, inspection methods, and nonconformance handling for connecting rod CFW-7434-20 (CFW-7434-20). It applies to all forgings produced at Plant P2 and covers finished machined parts prior to final assembly release. The scope includes incoming furnace-forged blanks, heat treatment verification, finishing checks, and final packing release. Background and rationale are provided to clarify why each requirement exists and how it maps to functional performance in service.

Requirements table
The following table lists the controlled attributes, acceptance criteria, and records to be retained for each attribute.

| Attribute | Acceptance criteria | Records to keep |
|---|---:|---|
| Material identification | Material traceability must link to mill certificate for CFW-7434-20 | Mill certificate and trace record tied to batch |
| Hardness | The hardness range for connecting rod CFW-7434-20 (CFW-7434-20) is 28-31 HRC | Hardness test report, operator initials |
| Bore diameter | The bore diameter tolerance for connecting rod CFW-7434-20 (CFW-7434-20) is ±0.11 mm | Bore measurement record, calibration stamp |
| Weight | The maximum forging weight for connecting rod CFW-7434-20 (CFW-7434-20) is 101.0 kg | Weighing log, batch identifier |
| Surface condition | Free of laps, cold shuts, and forging folds that affect functionality | Visual inspection checklist |
| Machining features | All critical features must meet drawing geometry and finish requirements | Final inspection report, machining program ID |

Inspection method
Inspection activities are organized to demonstrate conformance to the requirements table and to provide documentary evidence for release.

- Material identification and traceability
  - Verify mill certificate against purchase order and part marking for CFW-7434-20. Record matching identifiers in the batch trace record. Rationale: Ensures chemistry and heat history correspond to the part specification and downstream mechanical properties.

- Hardness testing
  - Perform hardness checks on representative locations specified by engineering. Use a calibrated Rockwell hardness tester appropriate for the specimen geometry. Report results such that the recorded values demonstrate whether the part meets the hardness range. The hardness range for connecting rod CFW-7434-20 (CFW-7434-20) is 28-31 HRC. Rationale: Hardness verifies heat treatment effectiveness and correlates with strength and fatigue life for the forging material.

- Bore diameter measurement
  - Measure bore diameter using calibrated bore gauges or plug gauges appropriate for the feature. The bore diameter tolerance for connecting rod CFW-7434-20 (CFW-7434-20) is ±0.11 mm. Record the nominal value and each measured deviation in the inspection report. Rationale: Bore concentricity and clearance directly impact bearing fit and engine longevity; tight control reduces rework and engine warranty exposure.

- Weight verification
  - Weigh forgings on a calibrated scale prior to material removal operations. The maximum forging weight for connecting rod CFW-7434-20 (CFW-7434-20) is 101.0 kg. Log the measured weight against the batch and identify any units exceeding the limit for disposition. Rationale: Excessive forging weight may indicate improper die filling, material overspec, or process drift affecting microstructure.

- Visual and dimensional inspection
  - Inspect all surfaces for forging defects that compromise function. Verify critical machining features per drawing. Use calibrated measuring tools and log all results. Rationale: Ensures parts meet fit and finish requirements for assembly and service.

- Calibration and equipment records
  - Ensure all instruments used for the above measurements are within calibration. Keep calibration certificates linked to the instrument ID and inspection records. Rationale: Measurement validity is dependent on calibrated equipment.

Examples and step rationale
- Example: If a forging measures within the weight limit and has acceptable hardness but the bore exceeds the tolerance, the part is subject to the nonconformance handling procedure. This maintains a consistent decision path and preserves component integrity.
- Example: If hardness tests on a batch show values near the lower bound of the range, increase sampling frequency and initiate a heat-treatment verification investigation. This prevents release of parts with potential low fatigue resistance.

Records to keep
- Mill certificate and batch trace record for each heat.
- Hardness test reports with operator identification and tester calibration identifier.
- Bore measurement records showing nominal and measured deviations, with gauge calibration reference.
- Weighing logs with batch identifiers.
- Final inspection report including all dimensional checks and visual acceptance criteria.
- Calibration certificates for all measuring equipment used in the inspection.

Nonconformance handling
Nonconformances discovered during any inspection stage are to be documented and controlled. The following process governs disposition and corrective actions.

- Identification and segregation
  - Segregate nonconforming parts immediately from conforming inventory and mark to prevent unintended use. Document the condition and the contrary requirement from the requirements table.

- Disposition decision
  - Acceptable dispositions include rework to drawing requirements if the feature is reworkable without compromising integrity, use-as-is only if authorized by engineering with documented justification, or scrap if the defect cannot be remedied. Document the chosen disposition and the approver identity.

- Root cause and corrective action
  - Initiate an investigation to determine root cause for process failures that led to the nonconformance. Implement corrective actions to prevent recurrence and document effectiveness verification. Keep investigation and action records with the batch file.

- Records and notification
  - Record all nonconformance reports, dispositions, and corrective action outcomes in the quality system file for the affected batch. Notify affected stakeholders, including production planning and engineering, when disposition impacts delivery or performance.

- Reinspection after corrective action
  - After rework or corrective actions, reinspect the part against the original acceptance criteria. Record the results and attach to the nonconformance documentation.

Approval and change control
Changes to this specification must be approved through the document control process at Plant P2. This revision is Rev C and supersedes Rev B. All previous versions shall be withdrawn from use.

End of document.

# QS-CFW-9335-36 Quality specification - gear blank CFW-9335-36 (8620)
Revision: Rev F  
Supersedes: Rev E  
Plant: P3  
Parts: CFW-9335-36

Scope
This quality specification defines the acceptance criteria, inspection requirements, and nonconformance handling for gear blank CFW-9335-36 (8620) produced at Plant P3. It applies to finished forgings delivered as gear blanks and to in-plant transfers to machining. The intent is to ensure material, dimensional, and hardness conformity before machining operations begin.

Background and rationale
Gear blank CFW-9335-36 is supplied as a forging blank for subsequent machining and heat treat operations. Controlling hardness and bore geometry at the forging stage reduces scrap and prevents downstream rework. The hardness requirement preserves machinability for subsequent operations while ensuring the material has not been over-hardened during cooling or post-forge handling. The bore tolerance protects fit-up in fixtures and alignment for machining centers. The maximum forging weight limit ensures handling equipment and tooling capacities at Plant P3 are not exceeded.

Requirements table
- Material designation: 8620 as specified on the part drawing.
- Hardness: The hardness range for gear blank CFW-9335-36 (CFW-9335-36) is 36-41 HRC.
- Bore diameter tolerance: The bore diameter tolerance for gear blank CFW-9335-36 (CFW-9335-36) is ±0.04 mm.
- Maximum forging weight: The maximum forging weight for gear blank CFW-9335-36 (CFW-9335-36) is 107.9 kg.
- Surface condition: Surfaces shall be free from forging laps, cracks, and conditions that would prevent safe machining. Surface condition shall be acceptable to the receiving process engineer.
- Identification: Each blank shall be marked and documented with the part identifier CFW-9335-36 and heat lot sufficient to trace back to mill certificate and heat history.

Inspection method
General
Inspections shall be performed by qualified inspection personnel in the Plant P3 inspection area using calibrated equipment. When there is doubt about acceptance, the receiving process engineer must be notified for disposition.

Hardness verification
Use a portable hardness tester appropriate for HRC scale and perform measurements at locations representative of the machined region. Report the measured values in the inspection record and compare to the hardness range. If readings are outside the specified range, follow the nonconformance handling procedure.

Bore inspection
Measure bore diameter using calibrated bore gauges or an inside micrometer capable of achieving the specified tolerance. Measurements shall be taken at locations that represent the finished bore geometry and aligned to the axis of the blank. Record actual reading and deviation relative to the nominal. Use the bore diameter tolerance for acceptance: the bore diameter tolerance for gear blank CFW-9335-36 (CFW-9335-36) is ±0.04 mm.

Weight verification
Weigh each forging on certified scales at Plant P3 and record the weight on the inspection report. Confirm the weight does not exceed the maximum forging weight for the part. The maximum forging weight for gear blank CFW-9335-36 (CFW-9335-36) is 107.9 kg. If weight exceeds the maximum, tag and segregate per nonconformance handling.

Dimensional and visual
Inspect critical surfaces and dimensions listed on the drawing for conformance. Visual examination for laps, cracks, folds, and scale shall be completed. Surface defects that compromise fit or function shall be documented and processed under nonconformance handling.

Calibration and equipment
Use instruments that are within their calibration validity. Calibration status must be traceable in equipment records. If an instrument uncertainty could affect conformity relative to the specified tolerance, repeat measurement with an alternative calibrated instrument.

Examples and step rationale
- Example: If a hardness measurement returns 35 HRC, this is below the hardness range. The inspector shall quarantine the part and initiate nonconformance handling with notation of measured value and supporting machine and operator records. This avoids downstream failure during machining.
- Example: If bore measurement shows deviation of greater than the allowed ±0.04 mm, the part will be segregated for review; machining fixturing may not accept that deviation and downstream rework could be required.
- Rationale: Specifying mechanical acceptance at the forging stage reduces risk of scrapped machined parts. Recording actual measured values provides statistical feedback to forge process owners for control.

Records to keep
Maintain the following records in the Plant P3 document control system:
- Inspection report with measured hardness readings and locations.
- Bore measurement records showing actual reading and comparison to the bore diameter tolerance for gear blank CFW-9335-36 (CFW-9335-36) is ±0.04 mm.
- Weight record confirming the maximum forging weight for gear blank CFW-9335-36 (CFW-9335-36) is 107.9 kg.
- Heat lot traceability and mill certificates.
- Nonconformance reports and final disposition records.
Records shall be retained according to Plant P3 document retention policy and made available for audits and customer review.

Nonconformance handling
Identification and segregation
Nonconforming parts shall be clearly tagged and segregated from conforming inventory to prevent inadvertent use. Tag shall reference the part CFW-9335-36 and the reason for segregation.

Disposition
The receiving inspector or process engineer shall determine disposition options which may include rework, remelt, use as-is with customer approval, or scrap. Disposition shall be documented in the nonconformance report and include measured values and supporting evidence.

Root cause and corrective action
For any nonconformance, perform a root cause evaluation to determine if the issue is process related, material related, or handling related. Implement corrective actions and document effectiveness verification in the nonconformance record.

Return to service
Only after documented corrective action and verification shall a nonconforming item be returned to production flow. Records of verification steps and approvals shall be attached to the part history.

Audit and continuous improvement
Inspection results and nonconformance trends shall be reviewed by Plant P3 quality leadership to identify process improvements. Measured values recorded against the hardness range and bore diameter tolerance for gear blank CFW-9335-36 (CFW-9335-36) will be used to monitor process stability and plan preventive actions.

End of document.

# SOP-P3-L3-02 Product changeover - Machining line
Revision: Rev F — This revision supersedes Rev E  
Plant: P3, line P3-L3  
Equipment: EQ-P3-L3-SB01, EQ-P3-L3-CN02, EQ-P3-L3-HP03

Purpose
1. Define the controlled process for product changeover on the machining line to ensure safe, repeatable setup and to preserve part quality and traceability.

Scope
2. Applies to operators, lead technicians, and maintenance personnel performing product changeover on EQ-P3-L3-SB01, EQ-P3-L3-CN02, and EQ-P3-L3-HP03 on P3-L3.

Background and rationale
3. Frequent product changeover on machining lines introduces risk of setup error, contamination, and torque-related failures. Standardized steps reduce scrap, prevent equipment damage, and ensure safety compliance. This SOP references machine-specific procedures and safety bulletins to align maintenance and lubrication actions with asset history and OEM guidance. See SB-1005 and SB-1010 for safety bulletins and SOP-P3-L3-04 for related tooling changeover.

Preconditions
4. Verify the following before initiating changeover:
   - Production schedule authorizes changeover and the new work order is approved.
   - All affected operators and maintenance staff are present and briefed.
   - All required PPE is available and inspected.
   - Energy isolation orders completed and documented where physically required.
   - Tools and consumables on the changeover kit are present and verified against the kit list.

PPE
5. Mandatory PPE items:
   - Safety glasses
   - Steel-toe footwear
   - Cut-resistant gloves for handling tooling
   - Hearing protection when machines are powered on for trial runs
   - Any site-specific PPE as required by SB-1005

Changeover procedure
6. Prepare
   - Stop production and secure the line following lockout/tagout procedures in SB-1010.
   - Clear all parts from the feed and unload areas of EQ-P3-L3-SB01 and EQ-P3-L3-CN02.
   - Visually inspect EQ-P3-L3-HP03 for leaks or damage and document findings.

7. Disassemble and swap tooling
   - Remove current tooling from EQ-P3-L3-SB01 and EQ-P3-L3-CN02 using care to avoid contamination and damage to datum surfaces.
   - Clean mating surfaces with lint-free wipes; use recommended cleaners referenced in SB-1005.
   - Install new tooling per the tooling setup sheet. Ensure datum alignment to visual and tactile checks described in SOP-P3-L3-04.

8. Press-specific checks (EQ-P3-L3-HP03)
   - Refit press platen and check alignment using the press alignment gauge referenced in maintenance records.
   - The main ram bolt torque for Machining hydraulic forging press #3 (EQ-P3-L3-HP03) is 1600 N·m. Apply this value exactly when torqueing the main ram bolt using a calibrated torque wrench. Record the torque tool ID and calibration stamp in the record.
   - Refill or top-up lubricant per equipment lubrication schedule using lubricant part number for Machining hydraulic forging press #3 (EQ-P3-L3-HP03) is CFW-LUB-254. Record batch number and quantity used.

9. Functional checks and trial run
   - Restore power following SB-1010 procedures and energize controls.
   - Run single-part trials through EQ-P3-L3-SB01, EQ-P3-L3-CN02, and EQ-P3-L3-HP03 to confirm part fit, dimensions, and cycle integrity.
   - Monitor for abnormal noise, vibration, or leaks. If any issue is detected, stop and perform fault isolation.

10. Quality verification
   - Measure first-piece characteristics and compare to work order tolerances using calibrated gauges. Log measurements on the first-piece check form.
   - If first-piece is within tolerance, proceed to low-rate production and re-check at the end of the low-rate run as per SOP-P3-L3-04.

11. Cleanup and documentation
   - Remove changeover tools and store in designated location.
   - Clean work areas to remove chips and swarf; apply rust inhibitor if required by the tooling spec.
   - Complete the changeover checklist and sign the shift log.

Examples and common failure modes
12. Example: If run-out is observed after installing the press platen, recheck the main ram bolt torque setting to the specified value and inspect for crushed shims or foreign material between mating faces. Re-torque to the specified value and re-run single-piece trials.
13. Example: If lubricant contamination is found in the hydraulic reservoir, drain per maintenance instructions in SB-1005 and replace with lubricant part number CFW-LUB-254. Record contamination incident and corrective actions.

Records to keep
14. Maintain the following documents in the electronic changeover folder:
   - Completed changeover checklist with signatures.
   - First-piece inspection records.
   - Torque recording sheet showing the main ram bolt torque for Machining hydraulic forging press #3 (EQ-P3-L3-HP03) is 1600 N·m and tool calibration ID.
   - Lubrication log showing lubricant part number for Machining hydraulic forging press #3 (EQ-P3-L3-HP03) is CFW-LUB-254 with batch and quantity.
   - Any nonconformance reports and corrective action records.
   - Tags and LOTO release records per SB-1010.

Sign-off
15. Required signatures and acceptance criteria:
   - Operator (changeover lead) confirms first-piece acceptance and signs.
   - Quality inspector verifies measurements and signs.
   - Maintenance verifies torque and lubrication entries and signs.
   - Production supervisor confirms line readiness and signs.

Revision and related documents
16. This document is Rev F and supersedes Rev E. Consult the following for related procedures and safety guidance: SB-1005, SB-1010, SOP-P3-L3-04.

Appendix
17. Contact maintenance for torque tool calibration discrepancies. Report any deviations from this SOP immediately and attach deviation approval to the changeover records.
